levels the planner refuses); the arc crossing law on a 3D level is proved on a

## M13.8: the fixture sweep walks the mid-move pose law, with a proven swing (2026-11-06)

**Finding first**: the fixture sweep did not sample only a move's ends -
`posed_steel` already cut each posed move into 0.5 mm intervals - but its
growth's swing term was the larger of the END poses' angles from the
midpoint, i.e. it ASSUMED the letter lerp never strays farther between the
samples than at them (true on an A-only geodesic, unproven on a combined
A+B lean), and it was a private copy of the interval law. Now `posed_steel::
sweep` walks `midpose::intervals` - the one law the part's solid (b2),
contact (f2) and posed-rapid readings walk - and each `Interval` carries a
PROVEN swing: each RS-274 letter turns the axis at most a radian per radian,
so from the interval midpoint every pose inside lies within ½·(|ΔA|+|ΔB|+|ΔC|)
of the midpoint pose; the capsules grow by `travel + reach·swing` and the
machine-frame rotary growth takes the same bound. The enclosure is
continuous between samples, not sampled. On A-only (4-axis) paths the bound
equals the old chord angle - no golden gained a warning; unposed and
constant-pose moves are byte-identical by construction; non-finite moves
still fail closed. Pinned: a feed whose end poses (−40°/−140°) clear a clamp
but whose lerp sweeps the holder through it mid-travel → FixtureHit once;
the clamp moved out of the cone → clean; under a 90° index the fixed block
(machine frame) is hit by the upright holder and the turning block (part
frame) is clean. Verify time on the rotary fixtures unchanged (11.5 → 11.3 s,
32.9 → 32.8 s). This closes M13.8's last owed item; the off-diagonal head-
before-table reading (rotary.rs law c3) remains the part law's only.

## M13.10: the area-control leftovers close (2026-11-06)

**The clipped finish's re-entry ramps along the kept chain** under the
guard's `entry_ramp` retry (`finish_entry::ramp_into`): the ramp starts on
the solid's top plane at `drop/tan(ramp_angle)` along the kept run and
descends vertex for vertex over the chain, so every ramp point stands
vertically over a kernel-certified centre - air by the 3-axis tangent law,
inside the centre area because the chain is; ramp feed = plunge feed (the
ring ladder's own choice). A chain shorter than the ramp, or rising above its
line, keeps the plunge and `center_cut_guard`'s named refusal ("even with
ramped entries"). A centre-cutting tool keeps its plunge, byte-identical.
Dropped: the 2D helix/`dive_room` law (it certifies against a level plane,
not a surface) and re-generating the finish inside the piece.

**Trace and Engrave take the group through `Native::ToolOn` / `Family::
Ride`**: containment and offset move the ride about its own chain
(inside/on/outside = 15/20/25 on the block, On move-identical to native),
includes and excludes shape the ring before containment as Contour's do; an
open boundary and an extension refuse by name (no ride edge to bound).
Defaults byte-identical (goldens 23/23). **Face's band under a 3+2 index is
built in the tilt frame and projected out** (`region_turn_of` returns the
local region + plane; `machined_footprint` projects through `world_region`),
so the preview is the cut - the overrun lands along the frame's u in world,
not 2r along world X. finish_clip.rs split for the 400-line law
(finish_entry.rs). M13.10 closes; M11.5's pointer stands.

## M13.11: IGES import waits for the M12.1 kernel - a decision, not a debt (2026-11-06)

**IGES is refused by name until the B-rep kernel lands (M12.1), and the
decision is recorded so no row carries it as an open debt.** IGES carries
trimmed NURBS B-rep (entities 128/144) exactly as STEP does; today's STEP path
rides truck's tessellation and every toolpath still reads a mesh, so an IGES
reader would have to be either a second tessellating B-rep reader (a third
crate's robustness and licence to audit, for a format the user base has not
asked for since M1.1) or a port of the M12.1 kernel's own reader before that
kernel exists. The clean diagnostic stays ("IGES is not supported yet - export
STEP or STL"); the M1.1/M1.3 rows point here. Dropped: a mesh-only IGES
importer (IGES mesh entities are rare in the wild; it would read almost
nothing real) and silently accepting the file (never). Revisit the day M12.1
reads STEP through its own kernel - IGES is one more entity table on the same
topology.

## M13.9: the rasters' over-read was the march's blind skip probe; a closed ring never flanks its own inside (2026-11-06)

**Not a partition, not a join row - the march's skip phase.** `ParallelMulti`
has no partition (both directions cover the whole shallow bounds). After a
run ends the march probed blindly at 4·δ₀ (4.38 mm); the strict tangency
leaves a fold gap of r·|Δm| between every pair of tessellated facets (0.2 mm
on the r20 dome, 0.47 mm between the hill's 9° bands), so a line is ~1 mm
runs with hairline gaps, and a probe landing in the next gap - or a
bisection converging on a later transition - dropped whole runs: the dome
Parallel's worst column had its nearest rows 3.39 mm = three stepovers
apart. The 0.349 "multidirection" reading was the single-Parallel path (that
test judges both). The skip phase now seeks from `tol` on a doubling ladder
up to the old cruise (open-air cost unchanged); the spiral family keeps the
blind probe, pattern-gated, because the ladder found an inner-turn piece on
the hill spiral and its newly flanked column read 0.156 against the 0.144
pin - a ratchet never rises. Readings (gate 0.1234): dome Parallel 0.349 →
0.125, dome multi 0.182 → 0, dome scallop 0.156 → 0.104, hill contour 0.231
→ 0.143, hill project 0.127 → 0, hill radial 0.127 → 0.126, ramp hill 0.297
→ 0.153, tilted ramp 0.170 → 0.170, dome flow 0.156 → 0. Ratchets lowered
or removed accordingly (dome scallop, hill project, the caller-less "open
dome geodesic" entry, the flow table); `finish3d_radial_dome.cl` re-blessed
(1958 → 1736 moves: one-transition brackets stop fragmenting runs).

**The ridge flank law needs feet from two distinct passes.** `ridge::
closed_ring_ids` names each closed iso-Z ring (its plunge and retract ride
the ring's id); `Flank::add` refuses an opposite pair from one ring - a
closed ring's own inside is one graze, rest's jurisdiction, not a cusp.
Pinned on the hill's crown ring (radius 1.62 < reach: 0.194 → ≤ gate) while
two rings at the ceiling spacing still convict. What remains over the gate
(hill 0.126-0.154, tilted shelf 0.170) is the strict tangency's fold annulus
r·Δm on coarse meshes - ground the march refuses by law, not spacing; the
next owed item is a kernel decision (edge-resting centres vs the belt's gap
law).

## M13.11: G41/G42 cutter compensation - the part contour under control comp (2026-11-06)

**`Compensation { Computer, Control }` lives on the contour's `Approach`**
(default Computer: every golden byte-identical), not a new OpParams field -
it rides links, undo, the project file (additive key) and the digest (a byte
only when Control) with no construction-site churn. **Control emits the PART
contour** (the region at stock-to-leave) under `G41/G42 D<tool>` on the
lead-in and `G40` on the lead-out - the variant G41/G42 exists for; the
"wear" variant (centre path, near-zero register) needs a register convention
per shop and is owed. The CL carries a `CompSpan` per ring (`cl/comp.rs`:
side, radius, first/last, the programmed moves) beside the cutter-centre
moves, which stay the sim/verify truth. **The lead law**: Control needs a
linear or perpendicular lead-in AND lead-out ≥ r, a closed ring, and the
seam re-seated mid-run on the longest edge so the control's engage offset
equals its cancel offset - the tool then runs exactly the proved centre
moves. Refused by name: arc/tangential/no lead, a short lead, tabs, corner
blends, overlap, keep-down links, open contours and runs, a 3+2 tilt. The
stream carries `COMP LEFT|RIGHT <µm>` / `COMP OFF`, the engine fires
`onRadiusCompensation` and refuses a script that lacks the hook the moment a
COMP record arrives; Fanuc writes the words, Haas/Mazak/Sinumerik/Heidenhain
and the lathe post refuse by name; every refusal blocks the gate. D = the
tool number (the library carries no offset register). Owed: the wear
variant, the other mill dialects, a generator-side concave-corner-vs-tool
check (today only the control's interference alarm catches it); contour.rs
stands at 415 lines (split owed).

## M13.11: cross-entity open-run stitching (2026-11-06)

**A second walk after the per-entity one, entered only for multi-entity
picks.** The runs the per-entity walk leaves are walked again across every
picked model (`stitch_cross::stitch_across`), welded on the same 1e-6
lattice in the op's frame (world XY, or the M11.5 tilt frame) with either
endpoint of a candidate matching (the flipped-continuation law), and
oriented by the same shoelace canon - so a rim split across bodies is one
ring (or, under an open boundary, one open chain), labelled "the stitched rim
of 'a' and 'b'", its picks consumed so the routing, chips and notes read as
the single-entity case does. A selection on one entity never enters the
second pass: single-entity output is byte-identical, goldens untouched.
Refused by name: a junction three runs meet at ("meet 3 ways at (x, y) - a
ring across models must meet end to end, one way on"; the picks spell two
rings and a guess gouges) and a composed ring whose Z span exceeds one weld
step ("lie on different planes"). Dropped: a looser plane tolerance (nothing
in the pick law names one) and resolving forks by the shortest ring (a silent
choice). Pinned: two half blocks butted at x = 0 with six rim picks → one
40×40 ring whose top-level cut equals the one-block cut move for move; the
fork and plane refusals; the open chain; create/set-geometry/undo/redo.
stitch.rs split (gather_runs / walk_ring / compose_ring; run_out.rs a pure
move). Found, not fixed: `contour_depth` fails closed below the top level on
two touching bodies (coincident seam walls) and says so in the notes -
tracked as its own row.

## M13.11: facing rows honour holes - Lift by default, Through as the explicit legacy (2026-11-06)

**The rows never change; the holes clip them.** The facer still clears the
bounding band (full-span rows, X overrun - `face_band_sane`'s doctrine); the
region's voids (holes less any island nested in them) are grown by the tool
radius - the pocket's cutter-centre construction - and each row is clipped
against that set by a half-open parity walk; the pieces are cut in row order
and a bridged hole is crossed by the facer's own level link (rapid up to
clearance, across, plunge at plunge feed). A row-end reversal or blend rides
only when both ends are whole. **`Face.holes` = Lift (default) / CutAir /
Through**: Lift is the only law safe without knowing whether a void is a bore
or a boss; CutAir cuts across air holes and lifts over islands (an island is
a void under material standing above the cut plane, `material_source::
standing_above`; with no outline to read, every hole is lifted and a note
says so); Through is the M1.3 band serpentine, byte-identical. Default Lift
costs nothing: no golden carries a hole and a hole-free region is byte-
identical under every law (tested). Refused by name: two bridged holes
closer than the tool ("the strip between them would stay standing").
Perpendicular leftovers beside a hole that only a tangent row could reach are
NOTED, not refused - the wide-stepover precedent; refusing would make the
default refuse every square hole. Dropped: snapping extra tangent rows into
the band (changes the row set, helps only rectangular holes); a tangent
cleanup ring around bridged holes is the follow-up if users want them faced.
Staged facing repeats pieces and links per level. The project file writes
`holes` only away from Lift; the digest likewise, so cached legacy faces keep
their digest.

## M13.11: mesh repair - weld by spatial hash, planar hole filling, one command (2026-11-06)

**`geometry::repair::weld` merges vertices by spatial hash within a stated
tolerance** (Teschner et al. 2003; pipeline per Botsch et al. 2010 ch. 8):
cell = tol, 27-cell probe, the FIRST occurrence is the representative so
nothing moves farther than tol; tol = 0 is a bit-exact merge. Collapsed,
zero-area and duplicate (either winding) triangles are dropped, vertices
compacted. **`fill_holes` is Liepa 2003's planar case only**: boundary loops
from odd-count edges walked as reversed half-edges (consistent fill winding),
a Newell best-fit plane, simplicity proven, ear clipping in the plane. A
non-planar loop (> 5 % of its bbox diagonal), a self-crossing or degenerate
loop, a non-manifold edge or vertex, an unclosed chain and a loop over the
budget refuse by name - a non-planar hole is NOT bridged with surface the
user never drew (Prime Directive); Liepa's full minimum-weight triangulation
was dropped for that reason. `open_edge_count` is the diagnostic, now in
geometry (the sim's twin). **`RepairModel` is the only door** (weld then
fill at construction, one undo unit over `UpdateModel` restoring the exact
previous facets and revision; `FromModel` stock copies follow); it refuses a
closed model ("nothing to repair") so no no-op history entry exists, and it
never runs on import. The Model page carries the verb (tolerance, largest
hole, the last report). Pinned: a split-seam cube welds 9 → 8 vertices;
a missing face returns as 2 triangles with signed volume +1; a 1000-edge
hole over a 256 budget refuses and fills at 1000 (cone volume π/3); NaN/
inf/collapsed soups never panic. Dropped: the sim's lattice-1e-9 weld as the
repair's law (bit-exact indexing after an explicit weld is honest about
what moved).

## M13.11: contour depth on touching bodies - the union of the picked bodies (2026-11-06)

**The depth ladder and the verify read a multi-model selection as the union
of its bodies**: each body is sliced on its own and the sections are united
by the 2D boolean law (`slice::material_above_of`, the same union the region
builders apply to picks across entities), so two models butted face to face
cut every level the one block they stand for cuts, move for move. One body
keeps the plain slice byte for byte (`bodies.len() < 2` short-circuits in
geometry, motion and sim), and a self-touching single shell still fails
closed at its seam with the floor note - fail-closed stays for genuine
non-manifold input. Two decisions: body identity comes from the pick's
ENTITIES (facet index ranges on the flat material list), never from shell
connectivity - two welded bodies share rim edges and cannot be told apart in
the soup; and the verify learned the ranges through a `verify_bodies` entry
rather than a new `VerifyContext` field, leaving its 35 construction sites
and every one-body verdict untouched. Pinned: the two-body ring cuts Z 10 and
Z 0 exactly as the one block (same moves, lengths, extents, warning count,
no "levels below skipped" note); the merged single mesh still stops at its
top level with the note.

(the lathe lift on the field and a headless binary per crate); neither left

## 0.8.2 hand-test fixes: edge loops, the Selection height offset, Outside containment, Circular from the selection (2026-11-07)

From the user's hand-test of 0.8.0 on testdata/models/Milling-test.step (a
60×50 block, Z −5..20, a round recess cut from the top to Z 0; the ~2500 mm²
face at Z −5 is the underside - not a shoulder, which changed the diagnosis).
(1) **Shift+click takes the whole face loop** an edge lies on (the boundary
picker's `extend_to_loop`, reused), Ctrl+click toggles one edge; the Edges
mode shows the hint and the open-run refusal says how to close the loop -
the multi-select existed but nothing taught it. (2) **The "weird height" was
the From combo carrying the old offset**: "Bottom of stock +18.7" (= Z −5)
became "selection bottom +18.7" (= Z 13.7). Switching to Selection now
starts at offset 0 - the picked face IS the floor. Dropped: converting the
offset to keep the same Z (the user picked the face to mean its Z). (3)
**Containment On/Outside no longer machines a hole of the part**: the part
was subtracted from the selection BEFORE containment grew it, leaving only
the recess, which containment then grew. Now the pocket kinds hand the whole
outline to the boundary step, only OUTER edges grow, holes stay as picked,
then the part is subtracted and only the pieces the band past the outline
touches are kept. Found, owed: Outside alone leaves a band exactly one tool
wide (2D Adaptive refuses it by name, "no room for an entry"), and 2D
Adaptive on an extended band planned for over 6 minutes in debug - tracked.
(4) **Circular fits its circle to the selection** (`circle_fit::
circular_fit_of`: the region's outer contour - or its single round hole -
accepted when every vertex is within 0.01 mm of the mean radius about the
area centroid); a non-round selection refuses with the deviation and where;
no selection keeps the typed circle byte-identical. The boundary group stays
refused for Circular (one change at a time).

## Issue #12: a whole-part Pocket source clears the stock around the part (2026-11-07)

Closes "M11.4 A+B" (6). A 2D Pocket / 2D Adaptive / 2D Offset whose
source is a whole part (Entity, not the stock) with a setup stock now
clears the stock's outline minus every part section standing at the
ladder planes - the M11.4 island law the picked pockets ride
(`area::whole_model_pocket`). A part covering the whole stock outline is
refused by name. Kept: a Stock source, the stock entity itself, and a

Dropped: refusing every whole-model pocket (breaks that documented

## Issue #42: the gouge law reads Area-mode moves along their whole length (2026-11-07)

The reported 0.30 mm "gouge" at the block corner was the pinning test
sampling a true G2 (R 5.000 about the corner) along its chord. The
generator was right, and the test now samples arcs on the arc. The real
hole was in the verifier: law (b) read a straight move only at its
`to`, so a G1 chorded across a convex corner with both ends R off the
part passed (1.46 mm in for the arc's chord, 0.30 mm in for a tangent
G1). Chosen: in `Mode::Area` (the pocket family, where every region
edge is a wall or an island), every chord is measured against every
boundary edge by segment-to-segment distance. Kept: `Mode::Boundary`
(Face, Contour, Thread, Drill, Bore) on the old law points, because a
Face's rows cross the face's open edge by design and the whole-chord
reading convicted them (two area_controls tests). Dropped: the
whole-chord law for every mode, and point sampling along the move
(a step size only shrinks the miss, it never closes it). Owed: a
Contour G1 cut across a convex corner of its own wall is still read at
its endpoint only; that needs open-edge awareness and has its own issue.

## #40: the control-comp room law - inside corners and necks refused by name (2026-11-07)

Closes M13.11's owed "concave-corner-vs-tool check" (`machining2d/contour_comp_room.rs`,
run in `push_span` on the programmed ring the walked centre ring pairs with). **Chosen:**
(1) every edge must hold the offset trims of its inside ends, r * tan(turn/2) apiece
(the controller's line-intersection rule) - a sharp inside corner between long edges
passes, a facet run tighter than r is named as an arc of radius `len / 2 sin(phi/2)`;
(2) every fitted G2/G3 that curves toward the tool must have R >= r; (3) the ring alone,
offset by r toward the tool, must stay one ring (`Region::offset`), the gap named at the
midpoint of the closest pair between the split pieces. **Dropped:** the brief's flat
"edge shorter than r beside an inside vertex" - it refuses legal 90-deg corners whose
edges are between r and 2r and passes 150-deg turns it cannot cut; the trim rule is the
exact one. Rings the centre offset drops (an island the tool cannot reach) are not
judged - computer comp skips them too. Two bosses closer than 2r (Outside merge) stay
on the existing seam / distance / `is_sane` refusals.

## #43: the Boundary-mode gouge law reads straight moves against WALL edges along their length (2026-11-07)

`sim::verify::section::wall_gouge`, after #42's Area reading. **Chosen:** in
`Mode::Boundary` every straight cutting move is also measured along its whole length,
but only against wall edges: every edge of the model section (material on one side by
construction), and a region edge when the section holds a probe 0.05 mm off its
midpoint on either side (a Face rim over air is open, a Contour outline where the part
stands is a wall). With no model there is no material to probe: a move that properly
crosses a region edge is read as overrunning an open rim (the Face row - a wall is never
crossed by a legitimate move) and keeps the endpoint reading; a move that crosses none
answers to every region edge. Arcs keep the law points (their chords sag inward).
**Dropped:** a new `Mode` variant or a `VerifyContext` field naming open edges (touches
every constructor and kind for what the section already knows); the plain whole-chord
reading of every edge (convicts Face, #42's finding). Known limit, model-less only: a
straight move that CROSSES a wall of a 2.5-D contour (centre inside the material) is
excused by the crossing rule, exactly as before this change. Note: the solid law (b2)
did NOT catch the pinned chord with the mesh in hand either - the tangency law was the
only line, so the fix is not redundant.

## #13: 2D Adaptive refuses a channel too long for one growth spiral, at once and by name (2026-11-07)

`motion::machining2d::adaptive::budget`. **Cause:** the extended Outside band round the
Milling-test part is a 14 mm annulus (D10): its centre area a closed ~4 mm channel ~270 mm
long, no star cell, so the growth rings (`grow`) slit it open and grow ONE spiral along
the C. In a 4 mm channel each revolution held the load at 0.12-0.37 mm of front advance
(~1.5 mm^2 of ~1100 mm^2 a revolution) while re-walking the whole cleared outline (rings
of 250-500 vertices, up to 7 trials on a 1.3 M-cell raster): margin 1.0 spent 140 revs in
9.8 s release and went Short, 1.6 the same, 2.4 runs toward MAX_REVS 800 - about a minute
in release, many in debug. The work grows as L^2 with the channel length. **Chosen:** (1)
an up-front least-work law - channel length `L = area / (2 clearance)`, fronts each
travelling L/2 at no more than the step cap (1.5 optimal widths) a revolution over rings
averaging L: `L^2 / (2 cap)` in tool radii, refused past 2000 r (the 60x14 slot needs
~110 r, the user's band ~3400 r, a fat 200x150 island pocket ~1600 r); (2) a running net:
the summed length of every revolution tried, all margin attempts, refused past 30 000 r
(the slot spends ~5800 r). A refused plan has no passes; `pocket_hsm` names it ("the HSM
plan is refused: the area is a channel 13.9 mm wide and ~269 mm long ...") and the Offset
rings cut the area - the existing fallback law, now 0.06 s instead of minutes.
**Dropped:** a wall-clock deadline (non-deterministic: a plan's outcome would depend on
machine load); making the ring walk incremental (the real speed-up, but a rewrite of the
trial walk across grow/raster - not a 40-minute change; open as follow-up if the
adaptive is wanted on long bands); refusing via `Err` (the op would fail instead of
falling back, against the named-fallback law). Known limit: a very large island pocket
(lb past 2000 r, roughly 250 x 200 mm and up with D10) now falls back to Offset rings
up front where it used to plan slowly.

## #45: setup navigation, operation labels and order (2026-11-07)

**Chosen:** Keep the entity `Name` as the stable command key, store a separate
editable label and an optional within-setup order on each operation. Existing
projects retain name order; the first drag assigns positions to that setup's
operations. The browser keeps one flat Operations section, sorted by setup
rank and then operation order. Its existing Setups row appears only after a
setup exists; setup navigation stays in the browser, with no new toolbar cell.
Dragging across a setup boundary is refused; changing setup remains the
existing explicit property edit. The project format advances to v50 so older
builds cannot silently discard the new program order and post a different sequence.
**Dropped:** Mutating the entity `Name` on rename (older undo commands would
lose their target), and a UI-only sort (the displayed order would disagree
with posting, simulation and rest machining).

## #36: the march rides convex folds on the edge - drop-cutter edge contact closes the fold annulus (2026-11-07)

**Chosen: edge-resting centres for convex folds between shallow facets**
(`finishing3d::edge`), the ball-against-segment arm of the drop-cutter
vertex/facet/edge decomposition (Yau, Chuang & Lee 2004; Hwang & Chang 1998).
`build_sups` keys shared edges by exact vertex bits and keeps, on one of the
two facets, the neighbour's sky normal when the fold is convex; `support_at`
and `support_grad` add the edge drop (closed form in the edge's vertical
plane) as a candidate, admitted only when its contact normal lies on the arc
m1→m2 and judged by the same exact `ball_clear`. Concave folds, mesh rims,
shallow-steep edges and knife rims (a cap's base disc only looks shallow once
its normal is flipped skyward - the arc test refuses it; without that test the
morph rode the cap's rim down to the 45° clamp) keep the strict tangency.
Release readings (gate 0.1234): hill contour 0.143 → 0, hill radial 0.126 → 0,
hill spiral 0.144 → 0, the three hill "with ramp" entries → 0, ramp hill
0.154 → 0, dome multidirection 0.125 → 0; tilted ramp 0.1698 unchanged - a
single plane, the hop path reads the same, so its cause is the shelf's high
rim corner, not a fold. Ratchet table down to that one entry.
`finish3d_radial_dome.cl` re-blessed (1736 → 1874 moves; plunges 246 → 150:
chords no longer break at the crests, the extra feeds are the chord law
refining across the edge arcs). Dropped: the belt's gap law (a slack in the
facet test - forgives a sunk centre on a convex fold, the corrugated belt's
0.0317 mm bite); vertex contacts (the vertex gaps are points the readings no
longer see; owed only if a fixture shows them).

## #17 (M11.3): the swarf pose-law leftovers - link count, re-entry audit, rim dip: five decisions (2026-11-07, Prime Directive)

Readings on the motion suite's debug blade (`swarf_pose_continuity`, the
16 x 6 capped tube; the "172" of the M13.7 entry was an earlier landing's
count, 153 / 234 after the normal-retract fix on the app fixture):

| run | air links before | after |
|---|---|---|
| swarf, debug band | 68 | 34 |
| ladder, debug band | 106 | 51 |
| swarf, full band | 93 | 55 |
| ladder, full band | 145 | 84 |

Lowest stated pose: -7.3 deg (swarf) / -9.4 deg (ladder) under level before,
level (-1e-17) after.

(1) **The curvature fit reads one sheet at a time** (`curv::CREASE_COS`, a
neighbour whose normal turns more than 60 deg off the facet's is across a
crease and is skipped). The first cause found: the fit's neighbourhood is
1.5 x 4 mean edges (27 mm on the blade) and its 64-neighbour cap fills in
grid order from -x first, so every facet on the -x half of the tube took
the -x cap's normals (90 deg round the rim) as curvature along the ruling,
read unruled, and lost the swarf pose to the lean law mid-line: a 75 deg and
a 105 deg air link on every raster line. Now all 192 tube facets read ruled.
Alone it moved the count nowhere (68 -> 71: the mid-line pair became a
line-start pair at the rim); with (3) and (4) together 34 (the hold in air took it to 23 but was dropped, see (3)).
Dropped: nearest-first neighbour selection (would make both ends unruled
near the caps symmetrically - still the crease read as curvature); a
narrower radius (changes every flow fixture's field for no law).

(2) **`ruling::analyze` keeps one verdict per facet** - a facet the fit
could not answer pushed nothing, shifting every later facet's `ruled` flag
and indexing the direction scan past the end (a panic the crease fix
exposed: the flat caps' fits went singular once their tube neighbours were
excluded). It now pushes `false` ("no claim").

(3) **The swarf hold** (`stamp_pose::hold`): wherever the ball is in
contact but the ruling does not speak (a level floor, a rim or cap edge -
the stations the lean law answers), a pose that would turn past
`LINK_TURN_DEG` off the held one keeps the held pose, if that pose is a
lean, not under level, and its flank is proved in air (`flank_clear`, the
stamp's own proof). The ball cuts the same surface under any pose about its
centre; only the flank could differ, and it is proved. This removes the rim
station's turn at the raster ends and most cap-ring turns. NOT in air: a
first draft also held the pose on the exit rise (a Feed off the part) and
reached 23 links, but the app blade's verifier read that posed feed in air
as an Envelope rest of 14.8 mm (`swarf_generates_blade_lying_axes_and_
verifies_clean`, `advanced_swarf_adds_the_coarse_rungs`); a feed in air
keeps the modal upright, so each raster end still links once on its exit
rise. Owed: let the exit rise be a Rapid (or let the posed contact law
excuse a feed that leaves contact along the normal) and the raster-end link
goes too. This is the "lead-out blend" option of the owed line in its
simplest form - no turn at all; dropped: a retract-height lift (it shortens
each link but cuts none), and a blended pose ramp over the line's last
stations (a turn on a cut, which the guard exists to refuse). Not proved
here: the heavy pivot5d envelope scan (release lane) - the hold's flank
proof is the same proof every swarf station already carries, but the scan
is the judge of record and must run at the next cut.

(4) **The rim dip is fixed, not bounded** (`stamp_pose::level_ruling`): a
ruled contact read off a facet's EDGE projected the ruling into the contact
normal's plane, which leans along the ruling by up to sin 10 deg, so the
pose dipped by as much. The facet's own plane holds the ruling exactly;
where that reading is level or above and its flank clears, it is the pose.
The pinned bound in `swarf_pose_continuity` tightens from -0.1737 to
-1e-9 (level). This also lets the hold (3) qualify at the cap rings, where
the dipped lying pose used to fail the hold's not-under-level test.

(5) **The re-entry plunge audit reads the already-cut sphere for a ball
tool** (`plunge_law::reenters_cut_sphere`, `first_solid_plunge_as` /
`audit_as` with `ball`, wired through `center_cut::guard_shaped` and
`plunge_solid::guard_posed` with `tool.kind == BallNose`). The owed line
said the audit read a near-vertical re-entry "by tip column rather than by
the already-cut sphere (a non-centre-cutting tool could be refused there)":
the defect is the false refusal. A link's re-entry whose incoming pose
lies within the core's 30 deg cone of the contact normal is axial, and its
tip column was never cut down the NEW axis (the pose turned), so the column
law convicts it - though the ball only retraces its own retract and ends on
the centre the last cut finished on. Acquitted only when all of: a posed
Plunge; its end ball centre equals the last cutting move's end centre; the
first rapid after that cut starts at that centre and ends where the plunge
starts (both within 1e-6). Every other plunge, and every non-ball tool,
keeps the tip-column reading verbatim (`swarf_reentry` pins both arms and
two misses). The retract rapid itself stays the verifier's to judge (the
posed rapid solid law) - the audit acquits only what that rapid already
answers for. Dropped: acquitting any plunge ending inside an earlier ball's
sphere (a plunge from elsewhere sweeps unretraced material on its way).

## #18 - M11.2 verdicts made final: oblique entries and Heidenhain vertical arcs stay chords: three decisions (2026-11-07)

(1) **Heidenhain keeps vertical arcs as 1 um chord fans - final.** The
brief recommended native XZ/YZ arcs; dropped for a hard reason. The
post is the TNC's DIN/ISO mode (M3.3 B), not plain language, so the
CC / C DR+/- spelling does not apply. The public TNC 620/640 DIN/ISO
manuals say I/J are the absolute Cartesian circle centre in the
working plane (not start-relative increments). An arc with axes off
that plane (`G2 Z.. X..` under a Z tool axis) appears only as the
spatial-arc case, with no stated rotation sense for the ZX/YZ view and
no rule on axis order. A native arc would therefore guess a direction
that can mirror, and a mirrored vertical entry gouges. The fan is
exact to the 3-decimal word resolution, so nothing is lost but block
count. `arc_planes::heidenhain_rides_its_vertical_arcs_as_chords_and_
never_switches_plane` now pins both planes: on the circle, the arc's
own sweep sense (G3 in XZ, G2 in YZ) and the exact end. Reopen only
with a documented sense rule, or with a KL-mode post (M3.3 B).

(2) **Oblique entry chords stay a chord fan with one note - final.**
G17/G18/G19 are the only arc planes ISO 6983 / RS-274 define. A tilted
working plane per entry (G68.2 / PLANE SPATIAL) changes the post's
frame for a single lead move, and every dialect would need its own
tilt-and-restore block pair and its own refusal paths. That is not
cheap and not safe for one entry arc. Already pinned by
`vertical_arc_entry::an_oblique_first_cut_stays_chords_and_says_so_once`.
The near-axis snap (M11.2 B (4)) still turns the cases that are
within tolerance of an axis into true arcs.

(3) **Finding, filed separately: the Heidenhain XY arc centre words.**
The post writes `I`/`J` as centre-minus-start increments (Fanuc
semantics). The same manual reading says this mode's I/J are the
absolute centre, so XY arcs that don't start at the centre's origin
offset may be read wrong by a real TNC. That is outside #18's scope and
golden-locked, so it is left for its own issue (#49, P0: wrong
output) and not changed here.

## #49: Heidenhain DIN/ISO XY arcs post the absolute centre, in its own block (2026-11-07, Prime Directive)

Primary source, read in full (not a summary): HEIDENHAIN "TNC 640
User's Manual, ISO programming", NC software 340590-07 / 340591-07 /
340595-07, ID 892909-25, English, 9/2016, hosted at
content.heidenhain.de (`.../TNC640/34059x-07/diniso/892909-25.pdf`).

(1) **I/J are the absolute circle centre - the post now says so.**
p. 260 "Circle center I, J": the centre is entered as "the Cartesian
coordinates of the circle center in the working plane", stays in
effect "until a new circle center is programmed", and is relative to
the last programmed position only "if you enter the circle center
with incremental coordinates". p. 128: an incremental coordinate is
written with G91 *before the word*; this post writes G90 in the
preamble and never G91. The manual's own full-circle example (p. 267:
`N50 I+50 J+50`, start `X+0 Y+50`, `G02 X+0`) is only consistent with
absolute centres. The old output (centre minus start, Fanuc's
increment) was therefore wrong on every XY arc whose start is not the
work origin - a real TNC would cut about a different centre, i.e.
gouge or refuse on its 0.016 mm circle check. Fixed: I/J are the
CL centre shifted by the work origin, exactly like X/Y (`wo`).

(2) **The centre gets its own block before the G2/G3.** p. 261:
"Before programming a circular arc, you must first enter the circle
center I, J. The last programmed tool position will be the starting
point of the arc"; every example in the manual writes `N.. I.. J..`
alone, then `G02/G03 X.. Y..`. Writing I/J inside the G2 block (the
Fanuc shape) is not documented for this mode, so it is not relied on.
Considered and dropped: keeping one block (fewer lines, smaller golden
diff) - undocumented, and the manual is the only authority we may use.
An arc reaching the post without an XY centre is now refused by name
(counted warning) instead of posting a G2 without one.

Golden diffs: only the I/J words moved (to a preceding line, absolute
values); X/Y/Z/F and every other block are byte-identical.
Pinned by `heidenhain_arc_centre::heidenhain_arc_centre_words_are_the_
absolute_centre` and `..._shifts_with_the_work_origin` (CW and CCW
arcs ~100 mm from the origin, so absolute and incremental differ; the
centre rebuilt from the words as the manual defines must equal the CL
centre within 3-decimal resolution, start/end on one circle), plus the
updated `arc_planes` and `conformance` goldens.

Left open (not this issue): the manual writes signed words (`X+25`)
and `N` block numbers with `*` terminators; the post's unsigned,
unnumbered style is the house choice locked since M3.3 B. Whether a
real TNC accepts that style is a separate question.


## #50: Heidenhain DIN/ISO block form, program frame and drilling - from the manual (2026-11-07, Prime Directive)

Primary source, read as a PDF (not a summary): HEIDENHAIN "TNC 640
User's Manual, ISO programming", ID 892909-25, English, 9/2016
(content.heidenhain.de `.../TNC640/34059x-07/diniso/892909-25.pdf`).
The issue named four items; reading the function overview turned up
four more words the control reads as something else, so all eight are
fixed here. Each was "would the TNC reject or misread it?":

(1) **N block numbers and the `*` terminator - fixed.** p. 130: "A
machining program consists of a series of NC blocks ... The TNC numbers
the blocks"; every program in the manual is `N<n> words*`. Unnumbered,
unterminated lines are not this mode's block form, so not relied on.
Chosen: N10, step 10 (the manual's own programs); a program long enough
for N to reach 99999999 (the end block's number) is refused by name.

(2) **Signed coordinate words - fixed.** Every coordinate in the
manual is signed (`X+0 Y+38.5`, `Z-40`, `I+50 J+50`; pp. 66, 131, 267).
X/Y/Z/I/J now always carry `+`/`-`; F, S, T stay unsigned as there.
G words are written two-digit (`G00`..`G03`, the overview p. 752).

(3) **Program begin/end - fixed.** p. 130: first block `%name G71 *`
(G71 = mm "at start of program", p. 755), last `N99999999 %name G71 *`.
The stream has no program name, so the machine's name stands in, cut
to the file-name characters of p. 143 (`VMC 3-AXIS` -> `VMC_3-AXIS`).
The old `(name)` line is gone: parentheses are no TNC comment (p. 172,
comments are `;`). Dropped: a fixed name `CAMCRAFT` (loses the
identity line for nothing).

(4) **Drilling - G81-G89 were wrong, and dangerously so.** p. 752 lists
the drilling cycles as G200-G209 only; p. 756 shows G73 is ROTATION
(`G73 H+45`) and G80 the tilted WORKING PLANE. The old peck
`G73 X.. Y.. Z.. R.. Q..` would therefore have been read as a
coordinate rotation, and the preamble's bare `G80` as a working-plane
reset. Chosen: no cycle word at all - every hole posts its expanded
chain (the generator's own plunges, peck retracts and exits, exactly
what the simulation verified) as G00/G01; a dwell is `FUNCTION DWELL
TIME<s>` (seconds, p. 456) right after the move reaching the bottom
(a dwell whose chain never reaches it is refused, never dropped).
Tapping is refused by name: plain moves cannot reverse the spindle in
step with the feed. Dropped: `G200`/`G205`/`G207` with Q values -
their Q meanings (Q200 set-up clearance, Q201 depth sign, Q202
plunging depth, Q395 depth reference, ...) are defined in the separate
Cycle Programming manual, not in 892909-25 (p. 71 shows only the
block shape), so mapping them would be guessing. Reopen with that
manual if native cycles are wanted (shorter programs, control-side
peck). BORE and BACKBORE are our own feed-in/rapid-out and
feed-in/feed-out definitions (`cl::CycleKind`), so the chain IS their
meaning; nothing is lost.

(5) **Work offset - G54/G55 were wrong.** p. 756: G54 is DATUM SHIFT
with axis values (`G54 X+20 Y+30 Z+10`); G55 is a touch-probe cycle in
the overview (p. 754). Chosen: the first work offset is the control's
active preset (no word); any other is refused by name. Dropped:
cycle G247 preset selection - its Q parameter is in the Cycle manual.

(6) **Tool call - `T.. M6` replaced.** pp. 71, 218: the tool call is
the T block `T5 G17 S4500*` (number, spindle axis, speed; it applies
the tool's length); M6 is "Tool change ... depends on machine"
(p. 392). Now `T<n> G17 [S<rpm>]`, `M3` in its own block; a speed
change alone is a T block of `S` only (p. 201). G40 G90 ride the
section's first positioning block (`G00 G40 G90 Z+250*`, p. 66), the
old standalone `G17 G90 G54 G40 G80` block is gone.

(7) **Homing - `/G53 Z0` removed.** G53 is DATUM SHIFT from datum
tables (p. 753); machine-referenced moves are M91/M92 (p. 393), whose
datum the machine builder sets - an M91 Z0 rapid could go anywhere.
The program ends `M2` and the end block, where the toolpath's last
retract left the tool, as the manual's own programs do. Dropped: a
`/` optional M91 retract (no documented safe position).

(8) **Judged harmless, left:** M8/M9/M5/M2 standalone blocks (p. 392,
`N20 M30*` p. 133); file extension `.nc` (the TNC's ISO programs are
`.I`, p. 143 - the extension is a transfer-time rename and the host
does not read it; worth a follow-up issue); no G30/G31 blank (only
needed for graphics, p. 131); no spindle axis when the stream has no
tool call (the active tool's axis stands, as before).

Golden diffs, reviewed by normalizing the new form back (strip N/`*`,
signs, two-digit G): every contour/face/pocket/slot/trace golden is
motion-identical; only the frame, the T block and the drilling changed
(drill_plate/drill_peck/synth now show the chain and the dwell);
`heidenhain/tap_plate.nc` is deleted (that golden is now a named
refusal in `conformance::REFUSED`). The Heidenhain synth golden posts
the synth stream with G54 and without the tap; the stream now carries
real chains (other dialects' synth goldens byte-identical). Pinned by
`heidenhain_block_form::heidenhain_posts_the_manuals_numbered_signed_block_form`,
`..._drilling_posts_its_chain_with_the_dwell_at_the_bottom`,
`..._refuses_a_dwell_its_chain_never_reaches`,
`..._refuses_tapping_and_a_non_first_work_offset_by_name`, plus the
updated `conformance`, `arc_planes`, `heidenhain_arc_centre`.

## #7 round 8: riding the corner pieces' leads as cuts fixes the island's hops; the spiral's own load near the island still holds it back (2026-11-07)

**Tried, the round-7 proposal**: `LinkLaw::ride_lead` (adaptive/lift_link.rs), the step
after `late` in `lift::schedule`. A late piece whose lead holds stock right up to its
first point starts at the lead's first point instead. Its lead is ridden at the floor
as a cut, the way the spiral rode it, so each lap shaves the west-wall sub-bite slivers.
That start also holds the slivers in the rim, so the cut begins further back, on the
walk's own path onto the previous piece: the previous piece's air lead where it runs on
to it, then the piece itself. The ride steps back 0 / 1 / 2 / 4 / 6 / 9 / 13 / 18 mm on
the exact walk vertices, never resampled, because a re-ridden stretch resampled at
0.25 mm posted segments a hair off the posted ones and the crossing law read them as a
crossing at (6.67, 34.60). The return onto it is `find`, else `high`. The ridden stretch
must read within `bound` on the stock as it stands. To reach the lift, `WORK_MAX` was
raised to 40,000 r locally.

**Readings** (release, `hsm_one` island 60x40 with a 12x12 island, D/120):
- **Baseline:** 9 hops (pieces 197..237 step 4, leads 24.7-24.9 mm), 4 highs, 1 ride.
- **Lead ride:** 2 hops (cap 8), 30 highs, 9 rides, 6 leads ridden as cuts, 620
  microlift returns. The ridden leads read 17-31 deg against the bound of 47.5.
- **The island now plans on HSM, with no ring fallback and the verifier silent.**
  - Out of cut: air 2,912 + lift 6,429 = 9,341 mm, against 8,221 mm in cut, so
    x1.14, inside the x1.5 budget. 61,848 moves, rest 3.5 mm2.
- **Not landed: the island now fails the judge's other laws.**
  - 176 in-cut breaks past 5 deg (worst 80.2).
  - 6 descents into stock for 2 levels.
  - The worst load is 125 deg = 79.4 % D at (43.66, 25.81), and the plan names it ("no
    step held the load somewhere - the least overload was cut").
  - The breaks and the overload sit round the island's NE corner (41-47, 26-34), in the
    spiral's growth, not at the ridden leads (x 5.3-8.4 on the west wall). The spiral
    itself already reads 125.0 there (the lifted plan reads the same 125.0).
  - Before this, `hsm_report_full_resolution` skipped the island because it fell back.
    Landing this would turn that lane red on breaks, load and descents.
  - The 3D stepped-block island level still falls back. `pocket3d_hsm` passes unchanged,
    so its reason was not re-read.
- **Budget:** not recalibrated. The island's growth needs ~31,090 r, and 40,000 was only
  a probe. That should wait until the plan it buys is legal.

**Chosen:** hold the patch (tmp/issue7-r8-lead-ride.patch in the main checkout,
including the 40,000 probe), keep the fallback, land nothing in code. The hop law is
solved by the ride. What blocks the island now is the growth spiral's load and kinks
round the island's corner. **Next:** the growth near an island corner ("no step held the
load"), then the extra descents (the 2 remaining hops plus high descents read as
descents into stock?), then the budget at ~32,000 r with the #13 band test re-timed.
**Dropped:** riding the lead from its own first point (that point holds stock in the
rim, so every return was refused); a resampled ride back (it reads as a crossing).


## #9 round 2: Adaptive runs on the rotary developed wrap - the M11.4 pin is lifted, refused levels are named by radius (2026-11-07)

**Chosen:** this round resumes round 1's WIP. `machining3d::pocket3d_air_split` no
longer rewrites Adaptive to OffsetRings. Each developed level now goes to
`hsm::plan_level`. The HSM planner either plans it, or refuses it as "the developed
level at radius R" and Offset rings cut it. The seam law (`hsm::Seam`) is round 1's:
under Adaptive, a centre component within 2*(r+leave) of a cover end that spans less
than one lap is refused by name. OffsetRings is untouched.

**Why the measuring changed (round 1's 0.0 % D):**
- The ladder's first level stands *on* the stock's own skin. `cut_levels` includes
  top_z = rho_ref.
- With the r6.2 clamp stock, that skin level is the only one the planner plans. The
  levels that cut material (5.7, 5.2) are refused on out-of-cut travel. So "0 % D" was
  true, but it proved nothing.
- Raising the measuring stock above the skin is no fix. The plan at the top level posts
  no entry descent, so the reading becomes a phantom 100 % D at its dive.
- The fixture now clamps an r7 bar, and is measured from its own skin. Levels 6.5, 6.0
  and 5.5 cut real stock and are HSM-planned.
- The reader also applies the bore law that pocket3d_hsm uses: planar moves inside a
  helical descent's circle count as entry engagement. Without it, the 180-deg readings
  were the helix's closing orbit.

**Entry:** Helix (r1). Under Plunge the planner itself named a 76.8 % D overload out of
the tool-size bore. Under Helix it names none.

**Readings** (release, turned bar wall r6 / neck r5, r7 stock, BN D6, leave 0.5,
stepdown 0.5, law 14.6 % D + 35 % = 19.7 %):

| Radius | Planar moves | Proved arcs | Load | Breaks past 5 deg |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6.500 | 22,528 | 8,694 | 19.5 % D | 0 |
| 6.000 | 22,528 | 8,694 | 19.5 % D | 0 |
| 5.500 | 7,416 | 2,620 | 18.8 % D | 0 |

- 5.000 is refused by name: the planning budget runs out after 86 revolutions, and
  Offset rings cut it.
- The planner's own overload notes: none.
- Every world move is posed radial, and no arc survives the wrap.
- **Load margin is thin:** 19.5 against a 19.7 bound.

**Rings digest:**
- Read on a build of db95014 *without* the patch: Helix (5263, 2919766036457321567),
  Plunge (5194, 6097177489831100083).
- Plunge matches round 1's patched reading, and the pinned Helix digest passes on the
  patched build. The rings are byte-identical.

**Lanes:**
- `rotary_adaptive::adaptive_plans_the_developed_levels_under_the_load_and_kink_laws`
  (~10 min debug) is heavy.
- `the_developed_window_reaches_the_planner_and_names_each_refusal` is a 12 long neck
  window. It still took 190 s in debug, so it is heavy too. Both run in about 110 s in
  release with --ignored.
- Debug keeps `offset_rings_on_the_wrap_are_the_program_they_always_were` and the
  seam-law unit test `machining3d::hsm::tests::the_seam_cuts_an_area_at_a_cover_end_short_of_a_lap`.

**Dropped:**
- An end-to-end seam fixture. A D-flat bar fails the axis fit's sphere guard when it is
  short (20 long). At 40 long it passes the guard, but the wrap's slicer reports "the
  mesh is open" at every level between the flat and the wall: 8, 4 and 16 dangling
  chord ends across three variants (flat through the ends, a closed flat across the
  seam, a closed flat beside it). The wrap development has not met a non-revolved
  feature before. That belongs in its own issue, not under #9. The seam law is pinned at
  unit level instead.
- A slimmer debug window. A 10 long window at a 2 mm stepdown still took 130 s. It also
  made the planner narrow the helix to 0.9 and then name an overload. That is a second
  finding to follow up: a narrowed helix bore under Adaptive.

**Review fixes (PR #57, 2026-11-07):**
- **The kink law now holds on the posted program, not only the developed one.** Under
  Adaptive, `wrap_exit` chords each developed XY arc at an angular cap
  (`ADAPTIVE_TURN_DEG` = 4 deg per chord) as well as the sagitta. Each end chord is split
  at 0.01 mm of arc (`trim_ends`), so a junction the plan held just under 5 deg gains
  next to nothing. The heavy test pulls the world program back into the developed frame
  and reads its breaks with the same reader. Readings on the whole bar:
  - sagitta only: 98,525 world moves, 12,824 in-cut breaks past 5 deg on the planned levels;
  - a 2.5 deg cap with full-step end chords: 138,097 moves, 14 breaks, all at arc
    junctions (5.0 to 5.9 deg);
  - the 4 deg cap with short end chords (chosen): 160,989 moves, 0 breaks.
  A 2.5 deg cap with short end chords also read 0, at 182,531 moves. OffsetRings keeps
  sagitta-only chords: its rings digest did not move.
- **A ring-cut level is now read from the program's shape.** It is a cut level (some
  cutting descent ends on its plane) whose planar moves have no proved arc. Such a level
  must carry the "Offset rings cut the developed level at radius R instead" note, and a
  named level must post no arc. The old check read "ring-cut" from that same note, so it
  was a tautology. Microlift heights (planar, nothing descends onto them) are not levels.
- **A hard planner error on the wrap now costs the level, not the op.** For example "the
  centre area has no room for an entry": rings cut the level, with a named note. The
  planar ladder still propagates the error. No cheap fixture reaches that error: any
  non-degenerate centre area has a dive spot, so no test pins it.
- The arc-proof tally note names "the developed level at radius R" on the wrap. Planar
  levels keep "Z ...".
- The rings digest now hashes coordinates on a 1e-6 lattice, so it is portable across
  libm builds. It was re-pinned at (5263, 11592310142122113043). On the same build the
  old bitwise digest still matched, so the lattice is the only change.

## Branch / PR flow for issues and cuts (user, 2026-11-07)

The user reworked the procedure: start each issue from the latest main on
a branch of its own; finishing an issue pushes the branch (PR), never merges
it; a cut goes PR review -> merge to main -> tag. Decisions taken filling in
the mechanics (AGENTS.md Issue Law and "A cut goes PR review"):

1. **Branch names** `issue/N-<slug>` (and `release/vX.Y.Z`, `docs/<slug>`):
   the issue number leads, so `gh pr list` and `git branch` sort by issue.
2. **A new `in-review` label** replaces `claimed` once the PR is open, and
   the pick query skips it - otherwise a pushed-but-unmerged issue would
   look stale after 4 h and get reclaimed. Dropped: leaving `claimed` on
   (stale-claim rule fires), closing the issue by hand at push (the law
   closes only from a merged keyword).
3. **Changelog rows are written at the cut, on the release branch**, from
   each PR's `Changelog:` line. Dropped: a row per issue branch - every
   open branch would edit the table's top line, so every second PR would
   conflict. The row names the merge commit and the PR.
4. **Merge commits, never squash/rebase** (`gh pr merge --merge`): branch
   commit hashes survive, so the `fix on ...` comments and `Fixes #N`
   commits stay findable. A branch behind main takes `git merge
   origin/main` (no force-push, which the law forbids).
5. **Review = a subagent that did not write the change**, under the
   Autonomous Work Law (the user reviews afterwards, not in the loop). The
   user can review or hold any PR on GitHub at any time; a hold is a PR
   comment the next cut honours.
6. **Docs/process/CI-only PRs merge once reviewed**, without a cut - they
   carry no behaviour and need no tag, and laws must reach main to bind
   agents.
7. **`release.ps1 -NoTag`** commits the bump and builds on the release
   branch (and refuses to on main); the tag is made on the release PR's
   merge commit after `git diff <recorded tip> <merge commit>` shows the
   trees match, so the zip is the tagged tree. Nothing else merges to main
   from the first issue-PR merge to the tag (a reviewer of this PR found
   the plain `release/vX.Y.Z` name is gone once `--delete-branch` runs, and
   a mid-cut docs merge would make the trees differ).
8. **Overlapping issues stack** on the open PR's branch (parent merges
   first, child retargeted to main), since fixes stay unmerged until the
   cut; an issue PR closed unmerged leaves `in-review` with a comment.

## #19: the lathe lift - turning programs on the field eye, about their fitted spindle: four decisions (2026-11-07)

(1) **The plan carries the nose and the fitted axis, re-fitted from the
generator's own facets.** `plan_program` no longer refuses the Turn family:
`stock_sim::lathe::lathe_plan` reads the op's source through
`operation::source_facets` (exactly `material_of`'s read) and fits
`turning::profile::Frame::about` on it - the same frame the kernels wrote the
moves in - so the field's revolved stadium turns about the line the generator
turned about. The sweep gained a stated axis (`LatheAxis`, new
`field_lathe.rs`; `Stock::simulate_lathe_about`; `simulate_lathe` keeps
`LatheAxis::Z`), and a chord's second end is signed against the first's side
(a parting chord past centre is 7 to -1, not 7 to 1). Dropped: assuming world Z
through the origin (a bar placed anywhere else would be cut 3.6 mm off in the
off-origin fixture); carrying the axis in the cached toolpath (a schema change
for a number the facets already determine).

(2) **Nose tools only; blades refuse by name.** Turning inserts and boring bars
(the nose circle) ride the eye; grooving/parting blades, threading inserts and
form gauges refuse with `LATHE_BLADE_REFUSAL` (#21 owes the blade-profile
sweep) - the nose stadium under-claims a kerf, and a picture that calls ghost
material the part is worse than a refusal. A lathe op's plan radius is its nose
(the display cell law `auto_cell` reads the cutting feature, not the IC).

(3) **The column verdict still refuses, by name.** `simulate_document` refuses
any lathe program with `LATHE_VERDICT_REFUSAL` (a Z height field reads a
parting kerf as a plunge); the revolved verdict at generation governs and the
post gate shows "not judged", as before. Rapids touch nothing on the field
(RS-274 G0, every arm's law) - a rapid through steel stays the generation-time
rapid verdict's to refuse.

(4) **Parity is the sign law at every cell centre, on generated programs.**
Readings (`crates/app/tests/lathe_field_sim.rs`, debug, default box stocks,
TEXELS 512k = 0.5 mm cell): facing 438,976 centres (10,680 cut) 0 sign misses;
facing about an off-origin axis (3, -2) the same counts, 0 misses; profile
rough+finish 438,976 (11,992 cut) 0; multi-pass contour 438,976 (9,160 cut) 0;
boring 429,777 (2,904 cut) 0. The sim suite adds a stated-axis case (0 misses
over the bar, NaN move / zero axis refused, a refusal writes nothing). The
law is written in the test, independently of the engine: air iff inside some
feed chord's nose stadium about the fixture's own axis.

**Review fixes (PR #60, 2026-11-07).** (1) The off-origin test now puts
the setup's G54 on the bar's axis (3, -2): the field revolves about the
FITTED axis, and generation (#62, its own branch) guarantees that is the
machine spindle the lathe post turns about - the module laws say so; the
refusal itself is #62's, not done here. (2) A chord whose ends stand in
different planes through the axis sweeps a hyperboloid whose waist the
flat meridian segment misses (less removed shown than cut): it now
refuses by name (`LatheAxis::chord_in_meridian`, out-of-plane offset
`|ra x rb| / max(|ra|,|rb|)` against `MERIDIAN_TOL` = 1e-6 mm), checked
up front so a refusal writes nothing; parting through/past centre passes
(antiparallel or vanishing radial vectors). Considered and dropped:
sweeping the true hyperboloid - the kernels only write meridian chords,
so a skewed one is a bug upstream to surface, not geometry to draw.
(3) A leaned-axis (10 degrees) parity case pins the general window reach
and the leaned split. (4) The laws state the nose circle is the whole
modelled solid (no flank/holder, unlike the mill's shank). (5) A milling
tool on a turning op gets its own refusal text instead of the column
engine's.

## #62: a turning op's fitted axis must be the lathe spindle, or generation refuses it (2026-11-07, Prime Directive)

The turning kernels fit their axis from the part's facets (any position,
lean up to ~89 deg), while the Fanuc lathe post writes X as the diameter
about the work offset's origin and Z as world Z. A part leaning a few
degrees in Y with its X on the origin keeps every move in one meridian
half-plane, so the post's off-meridian check passes and a taper is posted
silently (pinned: before the fix, a 3-degree lean faced and posted with
no script refusal).

1. **Chosen: refuse at generation** (`operation/spindle_law.rs`, called
   from `collect_job`) every turning-family op, and the lathe's axial
   Drill, whose fitted axis is not world Z through the op's work-offset
   origin - the same `posting::wcs_context` origin the post receives, so
   generation and post can never read two different spindles. The
   message names the lean (degrees), the offset (mm, at the part's
   mid-height), the slot, and the fix (align the part's axis with world
   Z, move the work offset onto it).
2. **Tolerance: one law, 0.0005 mm of radius**, measured as the axis
   line's XY distance from the origin at the part's lowest and highest Z
   (so lean and offset share one budget, scaled by the part's height).
   0.0005 mm radius is half the diameter word's last digit (X at 0.001 mm
   of diameter), i.e. a part that passes posts every word within one
   last digit of what a perfectly placed part would; an honest revolve
   fits far below it (measured in the review fixes, below).
   Dropped: a separate angular tolerance (0.01 deg was suggested) - over
   a 100 mm part it allows 17 um of radius drift, 35x the output digit,
   so it would admit a visible taper; a length-scaled single budget is
   the honest form.
3. **Lying axes and non-revolved models pass this door** so the turning
   frame's own refusals (LEAN_MIN "off vertical", axis::fit's "not
   revolved") keep their wording and precedence.
4. **Dropped: transforming the program** into the part's frame (posting
   diameters about the fitted axis). A lathe cannot turn about a leaned
   axis anyway; an off-origin plumb axis is fixed by moving the work
   offset, which the refusal names. Refusal is the smaller, safer change.
5. **Dropped: a post-side meridian check.** The post sees only points:
   a plumb frame's radial direction is +Y, so valid programs already ride
   the YZ meridian, and a leaned axis's points are indistinguishable from
   a plumb profile per move. Detecting it would need a new stream PARAM
   (the fitted axis), which changes every lathe stream/golden for a check
   generation already makes; the existing both-X-and-Y refusal stays as
   the post's defence. Only one lathe post exists (`fanuc-lathe.cps`).
6. **Field sim / verify**: on main neither reads the turning axis (the
   rotary kinds' `fixture::rotary_axis_of` is a different family); with
   generation refusing off-spindle parts, any sim that turns about the
   fitted axis (#19 / PR #60) and the post now describe the same line.
7. **Review fixes (PR #65).**
   - *Post-time door.* The stamp held nothing of the work offset's XY,
     so generating on a plumb bar and THEN moving G54 1 mm in Y left
     the op Ok and the post wrote every diameter 2 mm small. Now both:
     `posting::program_ops` re-reads the law against the live
     `wcs_context` origin for every turning op and the lathe Drill
     (before the freshness check, like the tool gate, since
     "regenerate" alone is not the fix), refusing by name; and
     `current_stamp` digests the selected slot's origin for those kinds
     (only when it is off the world origin, so no existing digest moves),
     so the op also reads Stale. Dropped: stamp-only (the post must not
     trust a cache key for a law it can read directly).
   - *Measure = rigid displacement.* The old law bounded the axis line
     at the part's Z extremes only; a lean `a` also cones every face by
     `R*a` (a 30 mm washer 0.4 mm thick at 2 mrad: 0.4 um axis drift,
     passed; 30 um coned face). Now every part vertex is read about the
     fitted axis (radius, station height) and about world Z through the
     origin (radius, Z); the worst disagreement of either word must be
     within 0.0005 mm. Equivalent to the reviewer's "drift at the
     extremes AND lean x largest radius", but exact per vertex.
   - *Fit noise.* Measured on plumb revolves tessellated like an STL
     export (uneven bearings, a micro-seam sliver, f32 vertices, at the
     origin and at (123.456, -78.9)): the eigen-only direction read a
     24-segment stepped shaft 0.0018 deg off, 1.1 um of radius - a
     FALSE refusal (2.2x the tolerance). Fixed by refining, not by
     loosening: `multiaxis/axis_refine.rs` solves the normal lines'
     Plucker concurrency rows (4x4 Gauss-Newton on two tilts and two
     shifts); the refined line is kept only past a 1e-12 rad floor and
     when the fit's own residual does not grow, so even revolves (every
     golden) keep their bits. Worst measured noise after: 3.3e-6 mm
     (~150x under the tolerance); 1.4e-7 mm at the origin. No real
     lathe STL exists in the repo's fixtures; the synthetic STL-like
     revolve stands in.
   - Wording: "posts every word within one last digit", not "the same
     digits".

## 0.12.0 cut: a test-only PR merged mid-cut (2026-11-07)

PR #69 (linuxguy123, `test(ui): serialize GPU render tests`, +6 lines in
`crates/ui/tests/gpu_render.rs` only) was merged to `main` by the maintainer
between the cut's issue-PR merges and the tag. The law (AGENTS.md "A cut goes
PR review", step 4) says a non-empty `git diff <tip> <merge>` means restart
from step 2. Chosen instead: merge `main` into `release/v0.12.0`, run the
suite the change touches (`gpu_render`) and record the new tip, then tag as
usual. Why: the change is a test file - the zip ships no tests, so its
contents cannot differ, and the full release gate (~50 min) already passed on
every shipped file. Dropped: re-running the whole release gate for six test
lines. The rule stands for any mid-cut change that touches shipped code.

## #79: the rapid law reads radial programs as a solid, not a column (2026-11-07, Prime Directive)

Why it was off: M5.2 F2 stood law (d) down for `Mode::Radial` because the
column (height-field) reading cannot see a horizontal bore - a retract
sliding out along its own kerf reads as lateral travel under solid stock -
and trusted the cross-drill kernel's traverse law instead. That made the
post gate blind for radial programs: #77's station change 5 mm inside raw
stock posted silently.

- **Chosen: a solid reading for Radial (`verify/rapids_radial.rs`).** Each
  rapid's flute body - discs of `r - gouge_tol` square to the pose at the
  tip and every 1 mm back to the flute length, walked under the modal pose
  rule (`midpose::intervals`, 0.5 mm of travel at the far end) - is tested
  against the stock prism (the footprint `Rest::in_stock` already reads,
  under the stock top) minus the kerf the cuts BEFORE the rapid swept (a
  tool-radius cylinder about each cutting move, extended back along the
  pose by the flute length when the move plunges along its own axis).
  Any sample in stock and in no earlier kerf convicts: `RapidInStock { at }`,
  the mill law's own blocking word. Retracts up a just-drilled hole and the
  peck's chip break are acquitted by the kerf - by reading the stock, never
  by the path's description of itself (the M13.7 swarf finding); the
  approach to a mouth on the stock surface is clear by geometry.
- The prism is unbounded below, the same reading the column law takes; a
  turned bar or box about the spindle is a Z prism, so the footprint is the
  solid measured about the spindle wherever the work offset puts it.
- Dropped: a `stock_bottom_z` field on `VerifyContext` (30 constructor
  sites, motion tests included, for a reading the mill law never had);
  sweeping the stack against the stock MESH with `SolidIndex` (the raw
  stock mesh has no holes, so every retract up its own hole crosses the
  mouth's facet - the kerf exemption needs point samples anyway); an
  unconditional axial-retract exemption like the mill's vertical one (an
  inward axial rapid is exactly #77's approach into raw stock).
- Not covered (as in the mill law): shank and holder bands against stock
  along a rapid - the flute body is what the law reads.
- Fixture finding: `drilling_cross`'s 44 mm box stock is REAL #77 - on
  main the kernel's part-measured approach stops at x 20 inside the x 22
  box and the hop slides through it (moves 0, 6; move 7 is under the box's
  Z 0 floor, convicted by the unbounded-below reading). The clean-document
  test now runs on a stock equal to the bar; a new test pins that the 44 mm
  box never posts silently (named RapidInStock, post blocked) and owes
  nothing once #82's planner hops outside the raw stock.

### #79 review fixes (2026-11-07)

An independent review of PR #83 found the law correct but costly and
fail-open at its edges. Taken:

- **Cost.** The kerf list is built once (cut order, each cylinder with
  its box) instead of per rapid; a rapid takes only the earlier kerfs
  whose box meets its swept box (padded by body + radius), newest first;
  a disc whose box misses the stock footprint's box (or stands above the
  top) skips the polygon test; a disc wholly inside one kerf cylinder
  (the retract riding its own hole's axis) is acquitted in one test
  instead of 25; shared interval ends are sampled once. Reading on a
  hand-made 40-hole pecked radial program (debug, `radial_rapids::
  forty_pecked_radial_holes_verify_clean_within_a_wall_time_bound`):
  **~9.5 s before** (1 mm discs) **-> ~0.25 s after** with the discs
  tightened to 0.5 mm (`BODY_STEP` now agrees with the module doc). The
  test holds a 3 s bound. Dropped: a per-point bbox inside
  `Region::contains` in geo2d (shared by every law; the footprint box
  reject in the radial law gets the same win locally).
- **Fail closed, by name.** A non-finite stock top or Z tolerance, or a
  tool with no finite positive radius, convicts every rapid
  (`RapidInStock`, the law's own blocking word); a rapid whose stated or
  held pose is no direction convicts itself instead of reading as
  upright; a cut with such a pose keeps only its tip's kerf (less kerf,
  more convictions). A zero or non-finite flute length reads as a body
  one tool diameter long, never the bare tip. Dropped: a new `Warning`
  kind ("rapids not judged") - it ripples into the UI's warning table
  and the project-file serde for a context generation never builds;
  RapidInStock already blocks and the move index names where.
- **Sampling bound documented.** Discs 0.5 mm apart, tip travel 0.5 mm
  between samples, and the 16 rim samples' chord sag `r (1 - cos(pi/16))`
  ~ 0.019 r: a graze deeper than the gouge tolerance by less than that,
  between two rim samples, can pass.
- **Tests.** Sim: past a drilled hole's bottom (flat end convicts), a
  tangential graze at half the gouge tolerance (clean) and twice it
  (blocks), a diagonal retract half in the hole (blocks), the non-finite
  context, the zero-direction pose, the zero/NaN flute. App: the radial
  tests moved to `drilling_cross_rapids.rs` (fixtures to
  `tests/cross_support/`, drilling_cross back under 400 lines) and a new
  deterministic `a_station_hop_spliced_through_the_bar_is_named_and_the_post_refuses`
  (the clean bar document's path plus one hand-spliced hop through the
  bar, judged by the real verifier, refused by the gate by move index) -
  it speaks whatever #82 does to the planner. The 44 mm box test stays as
  the planner-tracking twin (vacuous after #82, by design).

## #74: GPU adapter selection on hybrid laptops, frame-time budget (2026-11-07)

User report: Intel UHD + Quadro P3200 laptop never renders on the Intel
adapter, the NVIDIA chip does not take over, and the P3200 lags 1-2 s on an
empty scene. Chosen:

- **Adapter order** (`egui_app/gpu_select.rs`, pure, unit-tested on a
  synthetic hybrid list): inside each backend mask of the existing chain
  (preferred -> PRIMARY -> all), enumerate every adapter and log it (name,
  vendor, device, type, backend, presentable or not), then try: the adapter
  the user named -> the GPU wgpu's `PowerPreference::HighPerformance`
  request answers with (any of its backends) -> every other presentable
  adapter, discrete -> integrated -> virtual -> other -> cpu; ties go to the
  platform's native backend (DX12 on Windows, Metal on macOS, Vulkan
  elsewhere), then enumeration order. Adapters that cannot present to the
  window are skipped by name. Each candidate must give a device AND a
  surface configure that passes a validation scope; a failure logs its
  reason and moves to the next adapter, and adapters that failed under an
  earlier mask are not retried. When none works the refusal names every
  adapter tried and why, on stderr and in a native dialog.
- **Native backend before Vulkan for the same GPU**: on Optimus laptops a
  discrete Vulkan device presents through a cross-adapter copy to the
  iGPU-owned display; DXGI (DX12) does that natively. Ranking by backend
  inside the HP pick is the one change in default behaviour on Windows.
- **Surface config from capabilities**: the surface's own first format,
  Fifo (present in every spec-conforming surface) unless absent, Opaque
  alpha when offered else the first reported. Replaces get_default_config +
  a hard-wired AutoVsync.
- **Adapter choice setting**: `--gpu <name substring>` over
  `CAMCRAFT_GPU=<substring>`, the pattern `--gpu-backend` /
  `CAMCRAFT_GPU_BACKEND` already set. Not a world setting through the
  command path: the choice is consumed before the window and the document
  exist, cannot be changed live, and is per machine, not per project.
  Dropped for now: a preferences page entry (no persisted per-machine
  settings store exists yet - it would have to be built first).
- **Stall**: no blocking readback or `device.poll(Wait)` is on the idle
  frame path (the readbacks are test/diagnostic only; the traced-stock eye
  only marches with Deviate/playback armed). Not reproducible headlessly, so
  a frame-time budget (`egui_app/frame_watch.rs`) logs any frame over
  100 ms naming its phases (commands+scene, ui, acquire, encode,
  submit+present), rate-limited to one line per 5 s. The reporter's log
  pins the phase; the DX12-first ordering is the leading suspect fix.
  Dropped: switching the loop from Poll to redraw-on-input (changes
  playback animation behaviour; not proven to be the cause).
- **Review fixes (PR #76)**: (1) each candidate's configure, View3D build
  and a presented test frame (acquire, clear, submit, present, then a
  5 s-bounded `device.poll`) run inside Validation + OutOfMemory + Internal
  error scopes - OOM/Internal would otherwise reach wgpu's panicking
  default handler - and a device-lost callback flags a lost device, which
  wgpu 30 reports only through that callback; any of these fails the
  adapter by name and the next one is tried. Occluded/Timeout/Outdated on
  the test frame are not held against the adapter (window not presentable
  yet). (2) "Same GPU" across backends matches on PCI vendor + device ids
  when both are non-zero (DXGI and Vulkan name GPUs differently), the name
  only otherwise, so the DX12 entry shares the HP rank. (3) The refusal
  lists skipped adapters and empty backend masks, not "no adapter found".
  (4) The View3D pipeline is built per candidate: a failure there drops
  that adapter and tries the next, instead of exiting with no dialog.
  (5) `--gpu=x` / `--gpu-backend=x` parse; a surface-handle failure keeps
  the failures collected so far. Dropped: rendering a full egui frame as
  the test (needs the renderer per candidate; a clear+present exercises
  the same present path).

## #67: the cross drill measures about the work offset's spindle (2026-11-07)

`drilling::cross_drill` measures every standoff (bar radius, a station's
side, the hop/clearance radii, the station-change chord law) about world Z
through world (0, 0); the posts program about world Z through the work
offset's origin. Chosen: carry the job into the spindle's frame in a new
`operation/cross_spindle.rs` - the holes shifted by the `wcs_context` origin
(now collected once into `GenJob::wcs_origin`, the very origin the spindle
law judges), `stock_r` measured about that line, the kernel run unchanged,
the chain shifted back. An origin on world Z skips the shift, so every
on-origin chain keeps its bits. Considered and dropped: teaching the motion
kernel a spindle centre (a kernel API change for a frame shift the app seam
already owns), and re-latticing the shifted chain (it moved the kernel's
unsnapped chord points off the on-origin chain).

- *Spindle law for the mill-turn.* `spindle_law::turns` now also covers a
  Drill with cross holes on a mill-turn (the lathe's Drill was already in),
  so a revolved bar off its work offset is refused by name there too, at
  generation and at the post, and moving G54 stales the op.
- *Unreadable parts.* A plain lathe's cross drill refuses by name a part the
  axis fit cannot read as turned, as its axial drill already does. The
  mill-turn's does NOT: a hex or square bar is ordinary cross-drill stock on
  a C-axis machine, and with the standoffs measured about the posted spindle
  its envelope is honest whatever the part's shape (the drilling_cross suite
  drills exactly such a rectangular bar). Dropped: refusing it everywhere.
- Left open: the standoff radius reads the part's facets, not the setup's
  stock - a cross drill run before the bar is turned to size would hop
  inside the raw stock. Worth its own issue.

## #77: the cross drill stands off the raw stock, not only the part (2026-11-07)

Step-1 finding: on a mill-turn with A/B rotaries declared, an r10 bar in an
r20 raw cylinder generated Ok and POSTED SILENTLY with its start/approach at
r15 and its station-change chord passing r15 from the spindle - 5 mm inside
uncut stock (`G00 X15 Y0 Z10`, `G00 X21.213 Y0 Z10` -> `G00 X0 Y21.213 Z0`).
The verify crate's rapid-in-stock law stands down in `Mode::Radial`, so no
gate saw it (P0). Chosen: `operation/cross_stock.rs` measures the part and
the setup's stock (`GenJob::stock_facets`, the vertex hull: a box's
circumscribed radius, a cylinder's own) about the spindle and stands off
the larger; when the stock reaches past the part, each mouth moves out
along its own axis to the raw surface with the floor kept (the drill feeds
the uncut skin; the Auto cycle reads the true depth); the stock's Z top
feeds the end-face detour. Then every rapid of the chain is proven clear
(kerf retracts excused, the axial approach outside the raw stock, the
detour above the Z top plus the rim, everything else outside the radius
plus the rim) - refused by name otherwise. A stock that does not reach past
the part, or none (the op's source IS the stock, or no stock declared),
keeps the part-only chain bit for bit.

- *Stamp.* A cross drill's stamp now digests the setup stock (placement and
  geometry signature) - re-sizing the bar after generation stales it, so
  the old hops never post. Only that kind writes the term; every other
  stamp keeps its bits.
- *The proof found a kernel gap.* The quarter-turn chord law assumes mouths
  on the station's centre line; mouths off it (an (8, -6) / (-6, 8) pair on
  an r10 bar) chord 10.757 mm from the spindle, the r2 drill's rim 1.24 mm in
  the bar. Today that is refused by name; inflating the hop for offset
  mouths is a follow-up issue, not this fix.
- *Fixtures.* drilling_cross_spindle's world declared a 60x60 box stock
  centred on the world origin; read as raw stock it differs about each
  spindle, so that suite now uses stock-from-the-bar (its law is the
  spindle frame's alone).
- Dropped: bumping `r_d` by the stock/part gap (one number for all holes,
  and the kernel's margin follows `r_d`, pushing every hop out twice), and
  reviving the rapid-in-stock law in `Mode::Radial` (its height field cannot
  see a bore - the doctrine the sim crate states).
- Left open: a lathe cross drill is blocked at the post by "move 1 cuts past
  the finish surface" - `lathe_axial` is true for any lathe Drill, so
  `axial_warnings` judges the radial chain as a meridian cut. Safe-side
  (blocks), but a false refusal; worth its own issue.
- *Bit-identical, scoped.* "Bit for bit" is pinned on the existing
  fixtures; elsewhere the radius now read with `hypot` (where #67's reading
  took `sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2)`) may differ in the last ulp.
- *Stamp churn, once.* The new stock term changes every existing cross
  drill's stamp, so a saved document opens its cross drills Stale once and
  they regenerate - accepted over a versioned stamp (one regenerate, then
  quiet; a stale op never posts, so it is safe-side).
- *Review fixes (PR #82).* (1) An off-centre hole's mouth is now where the
  drill's edge nearest the axis (transverse `max(|t| - d/2, 0)`) meets the
  raw surface, not its centre line, and the proof's along-the-hole branch
  checks the swept drill slab (and, behind the flutes, a wider shank's)
  against the raw radius: r10 part, r20 raw, t 9, d 6, `r_d` 1 had the edge
  at r19.792 (0.2 mm in the bar, posted); now r20.956. (2) The proof uses
  the body rim `max(d, shank_d)/2`; the clearance and hop handed to the
  kernel are raised to `shank_d/2 + 0.1` in `cross_stock::body_clear` when
  the shank is wider than the drill (the kernel's margin is `d/2 + 0.1`), so
  a 3 mm drill on a 6 mm shank swings at z 23.1 over a z20 end face, not
  z 21.6 (shank 1.4 mm in it). Kept out of the kernel; a shank no wider than
  the drill moves nothing. (3) A hole plunging away from the spindle is
  refused by name in `to_raw_mouths`. (4) Found on the way: the proof read
  the opposite-station swing (which runs along the new pose's own axis) as
  an along-the-hole approach and refused every raw-stock opposite pair;
  the end-face check now runs first. Dropped: refusing a wide shank by name
  instead of raising the planes (a valid tool, only more standoff needed).
  Left open: the holder (`holder_d`) over the end face on a diametral swing
  is not in the body rim; the along-the-hole edge check covers raw stock
