  only (a part-only off-centre hole's mouth is the user's).

- *Review fixes (PR #78).* (1) Every cross hole must plunge TOWARD the
  spindle line: in the spindle frame, the mouth's radial offset dotted with
  the plunge must not be positive, or `cross_spindle` refuses the hole by
  name in world coordinates. The station law stands a tool on the mouth's
  side at the hop radius, so on a mill-turn block sitting off G54 a hole on
  the face nearer the axis, plunging away from it, parked the tool beyond
  the far face and rapided through the block. Chosen: the per-hole rule (it
  refuses exactly the holes that would collide). Dropped: refusing a
  prismatic part whose box does not straddle the G54 line (coarser - it
  would refuse the block's safe far-face holes too). (2) On the shifted
  path a kernel refusal is carried back to world coordinates (the hole's
  mouth point rewritten), so the user reads the point in their own model.
  (3) A lathe part whose fit returns a degenerate axis says so, rather
  than "its axis lies near the table". (4) A test pins that moving G54
  under a generated mill-turn cross drill stales it and the post refuses.

## #84: drilling refuses a hole deeper than the flute from the stock surface, and proves the holder clear (2026-11-07, Prime Directive)

- *Reach rule.* Every drilling op (cross and axial, every cycle) refuses by
  name a hole whose depth from the STOCK surface exceeds `Tool::flute_len`
  ("hole X is Y mm deep from the stock surface; tool T's flute reaches Z
  mm"). Chosen: the conservative rule - past the flute the shank enters the
  hole, and nothing models a necked shank's wall clearance, so a `shank_d <
  d` tool is held to its flute too. Dropped: relaxing for necked tools;
  measuring from the part surface (the uncut stock is what the shank hits -
  #77 moved cross mouths out to the raw surface, ~16 mm vs ~6 mm deep).
  Verify's law (e) (`flute + shank + holder` from the part entry, a
  warning) stays as the softer, later net.
- *Cross depth* is read off the spindle-frame hole list after
  `to_raw_mouths`: `-floor_d` plus `THROUGH_CLEAR` on a through hole,
  `min(SPOT_DEPTH, -floor_d)` for a spot cycle - the depths the kernel
  feeds. *Axial depth* is read off the kernel's own cycle records: from the
  highest material over the drill's (or a wider shank's) disk down to
  `bottom_z`. The material is the part's facets as they stand, plus the
  setup's stock clipped to the cycle's R plane (the cycle rapids down to R,
  so stock above R is the rapid laws' business, not stock this cycle feeds
  through). Conservative: a facet counts at its highest vertex when its
  projection meets the disk, and a stock declared over a part counts at
  full height to R even where a prior op milled it (drilling has no
  rest-material reading yet) - a possible false refusal on a pocket-floor
  hole with stock, never a silent collision. Dropped: counting the stock
  above R (every faced block whose Top Z sits under the raw top would
  refuse every hole).
- *Holder.* Read from the tool stack as modelled: the holder's face stands
  `flute_len + shank_len` behind the tip, `holder_d` wide, `holder_len`
  long; no holder modelled (`holder_d` or `holder_len` 0 - the turret-held
  kinds) means nothing to sweep. Axial: the face, `flute + shank` above
  the cycle bottom, must stand above the material top over the holder's
  disk. Cross: on every move (rapid and feed), the holder - a horizontal
  cylinder about the move's tool axis - must either ride with its lower
  edge (`z - holder_d/2`) above the stock's Z top, or keep the XY rectangle
  its footprint sweeps (convex hull of the eight corners) outside the
  stock radius `st.r`. The end-face swing between opposite stations is
  REFUSED by name when the holder would sweep the end face, not raised:
  the clearance that clears a Ø44 holder is the user's to set (a test pins
  that raising Clearance by 20 mm then drills), and a kernel that silently
  lifts the swing 22 mm hides a setup choice. Closes the "left open" of
  #77's review (the holder over the end face).
- *Fixtures that now refuse - real reach collisions.* The F2 cross bar
  (`cross_support`): its 30 mm through hole is 31 mm deep from the bar face
  (38 mm from the Ø44 raw box's face; the law reads 47 off the box's corner
  radius - #85) on DR-0400's 12 mm flute - re-ground to a
  50 mm long-series flute. `drilling_cross_stock`: mouths on the r20 raw
  bar 16-24 mm above their floors - flute 30. `blind_floor` and
  `solid_law`'s drill gouge tests drilled 14-15 mm from the z20 stock top -
  flute 30 there (they pin the solid/gouge laws, not reach).
  `operations::moving_the_part_marks_the_drill_op_stale_until_regen`: the
  block moved up 2 mm stands 13 mm over the stored through floor - flute 20.
  `operations::a_hole_deeper_than_the_drill_reaches_warns_and_still_generates`
  (M1.6: a 131 mm hole on the 12 mm flute generated with a ShankHit warning
  for the post gate to refuse) is overturned by this issue's done-criterion
  and becomes `..._is_refused_by_name`. `posting`'s warned-path test used
  that same fixture; its warned path is now a contour whose Ø8 shank over a
  2 mm Ø6 flute rides into the part's wall (the post gate's refusal of a
  warned path is what it pins). Verify's cycle-reach law (e) in practice no longer
  fires on a generated drill path (this law is stricter); it stays
  as the net for paths that reach verify another way.
- *Review fixes (PR #90).* (1) Tap, Bore and BackBore run in a hole that
  is already there (the kernel's solid-cycle door lets them by; the bore
  door already proves the cutting end fits), so they are no longer held to
  the flute: within the flute nothing but the cutting end is in the hole;
  past it the shank must fit the hole's diameter (`shank_d <= 2 r`), refused
  by name otherwise. The holder law still applies. Dropped: holding them to
  the flute (a 25 mm bore on BR-1000's 20 mm flute in a pre-drilled Ø12 hole
  was falsely refused). (2) The cross holder is judged per Z band: each
  move's holder Z extent (both move ends, both holder ends, its radius
  across the axis) against the widest part or stock radius within that band,
  each facet clipped to the band. A holder riding above the end face meets
  no material - the old global `z_max` skip falls out of it - and a Ø60
  flange 30 mm below a hole in a Ø20 section no longer refuses it. Dropped:
  the global stock radius (false refusals on any stepped shaft). (3) An
  off-centre cross hole's reach is the wider body's: a shank wider than the
  drill meets the raw bar further out than the drill's edge (raw r20, offset
  15, Ø3 on Ø6: 1.244 mm), and `to_raw_mouths` now returns that extra
  per hole for the reach law; the mouth itself stays at the drill's edge
  (where cutting starts). (4) A non-finite or negative `holder_d` /
  `holder_len` is refused by name (AddTool already refuses it; this guards
  any other path in); 0 still means no holder. (5) `meets_disk` skips
  facets with no 3D area, and reads a wall (no XY area) by its edges only -
  the same-sign inside test passed every disk on a wall's line. The
  cross_support fixture note now gives the raw box's true face depth, 38 mm
  (47 is the box corner radius, #85).

## #91: a drill's R plane below the unfaced stock top is refused at generation (2026-11-07, Prime Directive)

- *Proven P0 first.* An axial DR-0400 drill on a block (part top Z 20)
  under a box stock whose top stands at Z 25, R plane = Top of Part Z = 20,
  clearance 35: generation was Ok with no warnings, and the program posted
  silently through both dialects - Fanuc `G00 X0 Y0 Z20` / `G81 X0 Y0 Z12
  R20 F80` (and `G73 ... R20 Q12` for Peck), Heidenhain's expanded chain
  `G00 X+0 Y+0 Z+20` - a 5 mm rapid through uncut stock. Two holes let it
  by: #84's `top_over` clipped the stock to R ("the rapid laws' business"),
  and law (d) skips every vertical rapid as "a retract through the tool's
  own kerf".
- *Chosen: validate early.* `drill_reach::r_plane_clear` refuses by name,
  per cycle (every kind), a raw stock top above the R plane over the tool's
  body disk (the wider of drill and shank) - "R plane Z .. is below the
  stock top Z .. over the hole at (..) - the rapid down to R would cross
  uncut stock (a collision); raise Top of Part Z (the R plane) to the stock
  top or above". Axial only (the cross drill's mouths already stand off the
  raw stock, #77). With that law first, the reach and holder readings no
  longer clip the stock to R: the depth is unchanged over the body disk,
  and the holder is now held against the true stock top (the clip could
  under-count it by the stock-top-to-R gap).
- *#89 honesty.* The stock is read raw: a facing op earlier in the program
  is not credited, so face-then-drill with R at the faced height is refused
  too. The message therefore does not say "or face the stock first" (the
  check could not see it); it says faced stock still counts at its raw
  height. The refusal stands until #89 credits prior removal; the
  workaround is an R plane at the raw stock top (an air feed of the gap).
- *Verify layer held, filed as #96 (P0).* The net - law (d) judging a
  vertical rapid DOWN by its column (`to.z` below `Rest::surface_before`
  inside the stock is `RapidInStock`) - was written and green in
  camcraft-sim, but it is not contained: it convicts existing app fixtures
  that rapid below their declared stock top in non-drilling ops (posting's
  Contour1, retract 8 in a 10 mm stock; operations' Pocket3D shell test) -
  real collisions by their own stock, so the same bug class reaches every
  op, not only drilling. Fixture-by-fixture triage over all suites is its
  own issue; the patch and its tests ride #96.
- *Fixtures that now refuse, all real by their declared stock:* the lathe
  axial drill (drilling_axial, lathe_post: a 44 mm box at z 0..44 over a bar
  z -20..20, R 20 / clearance 30 inside it) - the box now sits on the bar's
  envelope, z -20..20, the posted golden unchanged; drilling_cross's Z-only
  file test (R 15 / clearance 20 under the Ø44 box's Z 44 top) - R raised
  to 44, clearance 50.
- *Dropped:* clamping R up to the stock top silently (a height the user
  did not set; the kernel never invents clearance).
- *Review fixes (PR #97).* (1) The R-plane law reads the part as well as
  the stock - its facets over the body disk and the hole's own entry
  surface (the modelled hole is what the cycle cuts, not air yet) - so a
  stockless op, or one whose source is the stock, no longer hands the law
  an empty slice: R 15 under a part top Z 20 with no stock is refused,
  naming "the part top". The message names whichever of part and stock
  stands higher. (2) A facet counts at its plane's maximum over the disk,
  not its highest vertex: the triangle is clipped to the octagon that
  circumscribes the body disk and read at the clipped corners (a plane's
  maximum over a convex region is at a corner; the octagon holds the
  disk, so it never under-estimates - at most r(1/cos 22.5deg - 1) of
  slope reach extra). A 1-degree drafted casting now passes R 0.3 mm over
  the local surface and its refusal names the local height, not the far
  vertex 0.4 mm higher. Dropped: sampling the disk boundary (can miss a
  facet corner inside the disk), clipping to the bounding square (41 %
  more slope reach than the octagon). The same reader serves the reach
  and holder laws (tighter there, still conservative). (3) Seeding: the
  drill's Top of Part Z stays seeded from the carried top (Top of Model
  + 0 by default) - not switched to Top of Stock. The seed has no world
  in hand (`retype_params` folds the old kind's numbers only), and Top of
  Stock resolves to nothing without a stock, so the seed would refuse
  every stockless document ("no stock yet") - a behaviour change for the
  no-stock case the review asked to keep. The UX cost, recorded: a stock
  with top allowance refuses a fresh drill's first generate, by name,
  until R is raised (picking "stock top" in the height field is one
  click). Revisit if seeding gains world access (a fallback reference).
  (4) drill_rplane asserts the refusal's words in the post path too and
  pins Spot / Tap / Bore, a hole beside the stock footprint, R from Top
  of Stock, the stockless and drafted cases. (5) drilling_cross's Z-only
  file fixture now asserts it generates Ok, proving the raised R. One
  more fixture was a real refusal by the part: operations'
  moving-the-part staleness test moved the block UP 2 mm under its fixed
  R 10 (the rapid onto R crossed 2 mm of part); it now moves down, the
  staleness pinned unchanged. The material-top readers moved to
  `operation/drill_top.rs` (drill_reach stays under 400 lines).

## #72: Linux release assets

- Build Linux x86_64 on Ubuntu 22.04 so the release binary targets an older
  glibc than the current Fedora workstation. Ship a portable TAR.GZ plus DEB
  and RPM from the same staged binaries and assets. The package installs its
  binaries and `assets/` together under `/usr/lib/camcraft`, matching the
  app's adjacent-theme lookup; short commands in `/usr/bin` launch them.
- Let the existing Windows release job publish after the Linux job succeeds,
  with the Linux outputs downloaded as artifacts. Dropped concurrent release
  publishers: both jobs would race to create or edit the same GitHub Release.
  AUR, FreeBSD, and Web/WASM remain separate slices of #72 because they need
  their own package or platform build paths.
- The macOS build uses one Apple Silicon runner to compile arm64 and x86_64
  binaries, joins each pair with `lipo`, and publishes a universal app in ZIP
  and DMG form. Resources stay in `Contents/Resources` and the theme resolver
  reads them there. The bundle is ad-hoc signed so both slices are valid,
  with notarization left for when a Developer ID and credentials are available.
  Dropped two native macOS runners: that would double the runner setup and
  make a single universal app require a third combining job.
- The Linux release tarball is the shared input for the Snap and Flatpak jobs,
  so packaging either format does not compile Rust again. AppImage uses the
  same release binaries and bundles adjacent assets with linuxdeploy; its
  download is pinned by SHA-256. The Snap uses core22 to match the Ubuntu
  22.04 build host and strict confinement with desktop, GPU, and home access.
  The Flatpak targets the Freedesktop 25.08 runtime and grants Wayland/X11,
  GPU, and project-file access. Both are downloadable release files; store
  publication and runtime validation still require a successful runner build
  and desktop hand test.

## #96: a vertical rapid down into declared stock is a rapid in stock

- **Law.** Verify's rapid law (d) no longer skips every vertical rapid as
  "a retract through the tool's own kerf": a rapid going DOWN whose end
  is below the surface the cuts before it left at its column, inside the
  stock, is `RapidInStock` (the held patch, unchanged). A peck or a later
  level's re-entry down its own earlier plunge stays clean - the cut-order
  chords acquit it; a retract up stays clean. Pinned by
  `crates/sim/tests/vertical_rapids.rs` (4 tests) and
  `crates/app/tests/vertical_rapid_stock.rs` (the contour under a 10 mm
  block is named at generation and refused at the post; over stock to its
  top it posts).
- **One false conviction found, fixed in the app, not the sim.** The
  turned family's Envelope kinds (ProfileRough/Finish, Facing, Chamfer,
  Taper, MultiPass, Boring) put the spindle axis on world Z, so their
  axial rapids are vertical in the column's eye: the column over a point
  beside the bar holds the blank (box or bar) all the way down, whatever
  radius the part or the earlier rungs leave - the column cannot see the
  meridian (the `Mode::Revolve` doctrine, which already stands law (d)
  down for the blade kinds). `operation/turning_rapids.rs` drops the
  column law's verdict on a turned path's axial rapids only, so that
  family reads exactly as before #96 (lateral rapids still judged).
  Considered and dropped: a `VerifyContext` flag (40 constructors across
  the crates for one family's carve-out), and switching those kinds to
  `Mode::Revolve` (it would also stand down their envelope and gouge
  laws). A meridian rapid law for the turned family is follow-up work.
- **No generation-time refusal added.** The common case here was not a
  clearance or retract under the stock top - it was an op whose `top_z`
  (5) sat under a taller block (10), so its plunge-height rapid (top + 2)
  dived into stock with clearance and retract both legal. Verify already
  runs at generation, so the conviction is named on the op the moment it
  generates ("rapid move N travels below the clearance plane inside
  stock") and blocks the post. A named "top of cut below the stock top
  over the op's region" warning would be friendlier but needs the
  op's region and earlier-op removal (#89) to avoid false refusals -
  left for a follow-up.
- **Triage** (every test the law newly failed, full app/ui/motion/sim
  debug suites):

| Test(s) | Op | Rapid | Stock top at the column | Verdict | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| posting: two_ops_post_to_one_program_cycles_stay_in_their_section, a_stale_operation_blocks_the_post_and_leaves_the_file_untouched, a_user_script_is_validated_on_choice_undone_cleanly_and_missed_loudly, posted_carries_line_positions_matching_the_move_chain, the_built_in_is_the_default_post_and_needs_no_choice, the_trace_rides_the_program_it_wrote | Contour1, top 5, clearance 10, retract 8 | move 1, Z10 -> Z7 at (13, -1) beside the 5 mm box | 10 (box 100x100x10) | real collision | `contour_and_drill` stock 10 -> 5 mm (the part's top); the Deep1 shank fixture likewise so its one warning is the shank |
| control_comp: in_computer_records_no_span_and_posts_a_centre_path_without_comp_words, the_lathe_and_the_other_mill_posts_refuse_a_control_op_by_name_and_the_gate_blocks, in_control_posts_the_part_contour_under_g42_through_fanuc_to_the_golden | the same contour | move 1, Z10 -> Z7 | 10 | real collision | stock 10 -> 5 mm; `contour_control_comp.nc` unchanged (stock is not in the program) |
| operations: the_shell_switch_sends_the_pocket_to_the_offset_engine | Pocket3D, top 5, clearance 10 | move 1, down from clearance | 20 (box 60x60x20) | real collision | stock 20 -> 5 mm (the cube's top) |
| motion pocket3d_hsm: an_open_level_holds_the_planner_laws, offset_rings_are_the_waterline_tiling_at_the_load_step | Pocket3D, top -5 | move 1, clearance 5 -> plunge height over -5 | 0 (the test's own verify context, stockless) | real by the fixture (the op says air above -5) | verify context stock_top_z 0 -> -5 |
| turning_bore: a_bored_op_runs_clean_in_the_document, the_bore_seed_stands, a_regrind_of_the_nose_convicts_through_the_digest | BoringTurning | move 0, axial rapid down the hole's axis | 110 box over a bored bar | false conviction (column vs meridian) | law: `turning_rapids` |
| turning_contour: a_taper_rides_the_modeled_cone_and_a_square_bar_refuses, a_chamfered_face_rides_clean_in_the_document, the_multipass_program_runs_ladder_and_springs_silent, the_seeds_of_the_contour_kinds_stand, a_nose_regrind_marks_the_rides_stale_both_ways | Taper / Chamfer / MultiPass turning | move 0, axial rapid | box over the bar | false conviction | law: `turning_rapids` |
| lathe_post: profile_rough_and_finish_post_to_the_lathe_golden | ProfileRough R1, ProfileFinish P1 | move 0, axial rapid (X13.7 Z25 -> Z2) | 40 box | false conviction | law: `turning_rapids`; `fanuc-lathe/profile_rough_finish.nc` unchanged |

  No golden changed: every .nc / CL golden matches byte for byte.
- **Review fixes (PR #105).** (1) *False refusal of programs that post
  today:* the column read only this op's own cuts and the raw stock top,
  so a face-then-contour (the face takes the block to the contour's top)
  or a pocket-then-drill was refused. Verify now reads the setup's prior
  stock too: `collect_job` collects a `rest::PriorPlan` (the stock grid
  plus the cached moves and tool atoms of every cutting op ahead in the
  same setup - the re-machining `ahead_of` law, program order by name)
  for every untilted, non-turned op; `run_job` cuts it
  (`PriorPlan::simulate`, the costly half) only when verify convicted a
  rapid, and `verify::acquit_by_prior` keeps a vertical dive's conviction
  only while the dive also ends below the prior surface - the same
  verdict as putting the prior in the column's min. Read conservatively:
  the highest grid column under the tool's whole disc; off-grid is air;
  no readable cell, an unbuildable grid or a posed predecessor the grid
  refuses = raw stock (conviction stands, the reason printed). Lateral
  convictions are not re-read. Considered and dropped: a `VerifyContext`
  field (40 constructors), and running `prior_state` for every op at
  collect (a dexel simulation per generation even for clean paths). The
  drill side: #91's R-plane law still reads the raw stock at
  generation, so a pocket-then-drill with R over the pocket floor stays
  refused there (that is #89); verify adds no second refusal (pinned by
  the sim unit test on a pocketed grid). *Owed:* a non-Pocket3D op's
  stamp does not digest the program ahead, so an earlier op regenerated
  shallower after the acquittal leaves the later op Ok on a stale
  verdict (not a regression - before #96 every vertical rapid was
  exempt); the fix is a live re-check at the post gate or the prior
  digest in every stamp (which re-stales every non-first op of every
  saved project) - for the main session to file. (2) pocket3d_hsm: the
  op's `top_z` is raised to 0 (the stock its load reader declares) and
  the verify stock top is back at 0; the ladder is unchanged (levels -5
  and -10, `LEVELS` and every pinned number stand). (3) verify's module
  doc states the vertical-dive law. (4) turning_rapids carries a unit
  test: one axial and one sideways conviction, only the axial dropped.

- The first AppImage crashed before `main`: linuxdeploy rewrote the executable
  and replaced its `.init` instructions with ELF header data. Assemble the
  AppDir directly and use the appimagetool already bundled in the pinned
  linuxdeploy download. The release job extracts the finished AppImage and
  compares its ELF to the built binary byte for byte. The Ubuntu runner has
  no graphics adapter for a headless launch; the desktop run was checked on
  Fedora.

## #71: the lathe axis fit sets off-centre features aside (2026-11-07, Prime Directive)

**Chosen.** `axis::fit` keeps its plain least-squares concurrency fit and
then reweighs it (new `multiaxis/axis_robust.rs`): the facets whose normal
lines meet the candidate axis within the fit's own concurrency tolerance
(`REL_TOL * rho`, 3 % of the mean radius) are the revolved surface; the rest
(keyway walls, cross-hole walls) get weight 0 and the line plus its
direction refinement are refitted on the inliers, up to 4 rounds until the
inlier set stops changing. The refit must pass the full judgement on every
facet (the 90 % concurrency share and coarseness gates), so it only moves an
axis the part already earns. Nothing set aside -> the plain fit returns
untouched (bit-identical; every rotary/turning golden stands). Guard: inliers
under 50 % of the answering area or under 8 facets -> plain fit, marked
untrusted. The guard is a backstop: it rarely fires, because `judge` already
requires a 90 % concurrency share, so a part the plain fit earned seldom loses
half its area to the trim. `axis::fit_report` exposes the plain axis, the set-aside share and
the trust bit; the spindle law names the share and gives the move-the-offset
advice only for a trusted (misplaced) reading - an untrusted one says the
reading is biased by off-centre features and moving the work offset may not
fix it (the share is of the turned, non-end-face surface). A trusted pass
with more than 0.05 % set aside generates with a named, non-blocking path
note (keyways, flats, holes, eccentric sections are not turned - machine them
in a later setup), so an eccentric pin turned as a concentric cylinder is
never silent; a plain revolve carries no note. Measured on a 72-segment D20 shaft with a
10 mm-long keyway: plain fit 0.153 mm (5.18 mm key) / 0.058 mm (10 mm key)
off G54, robust fit 0.000 mm.

**Considered, dropped.** A soft (Huber/Tukey) weight: needs a scale estimate
and never reaches exactly zero residual, so a keyed shaft would still read a
few microns off; the hard trim reaches the exact axis on circumcenter-anchored
facets. RANSAC sampling: nondeterministic and unnecessary when the plain fit
is already within tolerance of the true axis. Loosening `OK_SHARE` so parts
with more than 10 % off-axis area are read: out of scope - a part whose plain
fit misses by more than the concurrency tolerance is still refused as not
revolved (follow-up material if users hit it with long keyways).

## #72: Arch Linux source package

- Add a `camcraft` source recipe under `aur/`, pinned to tag `v0.12.1` and
  the source archive's SHA-256. Arch builds against its own libraries, and the
  tag includes `Cargo.lock`; `prepare()` fetches locked Rust dependencies and
  `build()` runs offline. Keep the binary, CLI, and adjacent assets under
  `/usr/lib/camcraft` with commands in `/usr/bin`, as in the DEB and RPM.
  Dropped `camcraft-bin` for this slice: the current GitHub release has no
  Linux binary asset for every patch tag, while a source tag exists. The AUR
  entry itself will be published after an Arch build validates the recipe.
- Validate `aur/` in a separate manually dispatched workflow on an Arch Linux container:
  compare `makepkg --printsrcinfo` with the checked-in `.SRCINFO`, run
  `makepkg` through its build and test stages, inspect the package contents,
  and upload the result. Keep this out of `release.yml` because the source
  recipe follows tagged versions and AUR updates, while `release.yml`
  assembles assets only for a CamCraft release. Manual dispatch also follows
  the repository policy against running Actions for every PR.
- The first Arch build reached `ld.lld` but could not resolve Flecs C symbols.
  The likely cause is makepkg's default LTO compiling the bundled Flecs C into
  GCC LTO objects that rust-lld cannot consume. Set `options=('!lto')` in the
  package recipe, as the Arch Rust package guidelines prescribe for mixed
  Rust/C projects, and verify the fix with another Arch package build.

## #80: the axial-hole verdict judges axial holes only

- `lathe_axial` (generate.rs) is now true only for a lathe Drill whose cross
  list is empty. A lathe cross drill already ran `Mode::Radial` (the mode
  match tests the cross list first), but the shared verify tail still ran
  `drilling::axial_warnings` on it, and that verdict convicts any chain without
  canned cycles. As a result, every lathe cross drill was blocked ("move 1 cuts
  past the finish surface").
- Laws a lathe cross drill still goes through: the #62 spindle law sits at
  the job and post seam (`spindle_law::turns`) and does not read
  `lathe_axial`. The #67 `cross_spindle::lathe_reads` and the cross kernel
  call, the #77 raw-stock standoffs and `rapids_clear`, and the #84
  `cross_reach` and `cross_holder` all run in the cross arm, which never read
  `lathe_axial`. The #79 radial rapids law runs in verify `Mode::Radial`. The
  #91 R-plane law is axial-only (`axial_reach`), so it does not apply to a
  radial hole. The change removes none of these.
- Mixed lists (Z holes and cross holes in one Drill op) stay refused by name
  at the cross arm's existing door ("not both"). That refusal fires before
  any verdict, so no hole is judged by the other kind's law. Dropped: judging
  each hole by its own kind inside one op. One program would then tell two
  stories about where the tool stands, which M5.2 v1 already refused, and the
  user can split the op in two.

## #85: a cross hole enters the stock where its own line meets it

- Each cross hole's mouth is now where the drill's body, moving in along
  the hole's own line, first meets the raw stock mesh
  (`cross_entry::entry`, spindle frame). It no longer sits where the line
  meets the stock's circumscribed radius. A 60 x 60 box therefore enters at
  its r30 face, not at the r42.43 corner circle. The reach depth (#84) and
  the Auto peck plan are measured from that face. As a result, a 30 mm-deep
  hole from the face of a 44 mm square bar reads 30 mm and posts on a
  35 mm flute (it was refused at 39.1 mm).
- The body is read as a square tube of half-width d/2 about the line, in XY
  and in Z. The tube contains the round drill, so the outermost stock point
  inside it is never nearer the axis than the drill's true first contact:
  the entry errs on the safe side. #77's rule holds because the tube's edge
  nearest the axis is what meets the surface first. The shank's added
  reach (#84) is read the same way at the shank's half-width.
- A round bar is unchanged bit for bit. The mesh reading replaces the
  circumscribed one only when the edge point at the mesh crossing stands
  more than `raw (1 - cos(pi/16))` (about 1.9 % of the radius) inside it.
  A turned bar's facets are chords lying inside the real round bar, and
  trusting them would put the mouth inside the metal. That band covers
  any polygon with 16 or more sides; the stock cylinder has 32. A tube
  that meets no facet also falls back to the circumscribed reading.
  Dropped: always trusting the mesh. That is unsafe on tessellated
  rounds, especially on grazing off-centre lines where the along-line
  error is many times the sagitta.
- The rapid proof (`rapids_clear`) now judges a rapid along a hole's own
  line against that same per-line entry, with the drill at its tip and a
  wider shank one flute length behind it. Before, it was judged against
  the circumscribed radius, which would have refused every box approach.
  Every other rapid (station-change chords, hops, the start/end planes)
  still stands off the circumscribed radius plus the body's rim. The
  kernel's hop and clearance planes are still built on it too, so the
  swing around the bar clears the box corners.
- `cross_holder` is unchanged: it still reads the widest material radius
  in the holder's Z band (circumscribed). This errs on the safe side. With
  mouths now nearer the axis, it could refuse a holder that a per-line
  reading would pass. That is left as a possible false refusal, not a
  collision, and can be filed if a user hits it.
- Review fixes (PR #120):
  - The band was measured against the GLOBAL raw radius, so a round well
    inside it (a stepped bar's d40 section under a d60 step, a cylinder
    stock off the spindle axis, a round boss on a block) was read at its
    chords on grazing lines: the mouth inside metal, the #84 reach short.
    Each facet is now read as its sagitta slab: thickened either side by
    `(h/2) tan(theta/2)`, `theta` the dihedral angle to an edge
    neighbour (|cos|, so a flipped winding hides nothing) and `h` the
    facet's width across that edge - twice the inscribed polygon's
    `(h/2) tan(theta/4)`, an upper bound however narrow the neighbour.
    Dihedrals above 45 degrees are real edges (box 90, hex 60): those
    facets stay exact, so box faces and hex flats read exactly. A round
    bar stays bit for bit: the slab only raises the crossing, which only
    deepens the fall-back to the circumscribed reading (the fingerprint
    test, re-run on the pre-#85 parent 2037891, passes with the same
    values).
    Dropped: trusting a facet only when its normal is parallel to the
    line (a tessellated round has such facets too); falling back to the
    corner circle (the pre-#85 air on every stepped bar).
    Accepted conservatism: an octagon reads as a coarse round, and a flat
    face bordering a tessellated fillet takes that crease's allowance
    (air, capped by the circumscribed reading, never metal). A round
    whose facets share no vertices gets no allowance - a known gap for
    non-conforming STLs.
  - The per-line entry reads the part's facets beside the stock's: a
    part poking out of a box face (a modelling error) still bounds the
    mouth and the along-line rapids.
  - The shank branch of the along-line proof cannot refuse a chain the
    #84 reach law passed (depth to the shank's meeting point <= flute
    means the shank stands outside it at the feed entry); its test pins
    the passing side on box stock.

## #89 - drilling reads what the setup's earlier operations removed (2026-11-07)

- **Chosen:** the axial drill's reach (#84), R-plane (#91) and holder
  laws read the stock top over each disk as min(raw stock, prior
  surface), the prior being #96's `rest::PriorPlan` - the setup's stock
  grid cut by every earlier op's cached moves - read conservatively at
  the highest covered cell (`verify::prior_surface`, now public); an
  unknown cell, an ungenerated predecessor or a posed (tilted) one that
  the column engine refuses all leave the raw stock. The hole's own
  mouth is lowered by the same reading (a counterbore cut first is air).
  The plan is simulated lazily (`operation::drill_prior::PriorCell`):
  only when the raw reading refuses, and at most once per job - verify's
  #96 acquittal shares the same cell.
- **Lathe:** a lathe axial drill reads the grid revolved about the axis
  (the lowest of four compass cells per ring, the highest ring) - the
  spindle carries any cut all the way round. A turning predecessor is
  now cut in the prior plan as its nose ball (moves carry the nose
  centre), not as a flat disc of the insert size, so a facing pass reads
  the faced end, never below it (a few microns high on the grid).
  `prior_state` (the Pocket3D rest mask) keeps its old atom - #109 scope.
- **Cross drills keep the raw stock:** the column grid stands along Z
  and cannot be read along a radial hole line; their laws say nothing
  new.
- **Staleness:** the Drill stamp carries `rest::prior_digest` (as
  Pocket3D's does) and `stale_reason` names the predecessor, so a drill
  judged against an earlier pocket goes Stale when that pocket's
  recorded path moves. Only Drill joins (#109 owns the general case).
  Cost: a drill behind any cutting op now regenerates after it - the
  posting suite's stale test regenerates in program order.
- **Dropped:** reading the prior always (pays a simulation on every
  clean job); reading the lathe grid unrevolved (a facing pass at Y 0
  never covers the drill's disk); a tolerance on the prior reading to
  pass R exactly at a ball-faced end (the reading may never be low).
- **Found:** the lathe Facing kind faces the work MODEL, not stock
  above it ("nothing to face" when the part top is the finished end),
  so a bar's facing allowance in the stock cannot be faced off yet -
  the lathe test models the allowance on the bar.
- **Review fixes (PR #123):** (B1/B2) on a lathe the prior plan credits
  ONLY the Facing kind cut with its nose ball - a boring bar, groove or
  parting blade was cut as a full-diameter disc on the y = 0 strip and
  revolved round the bar, and the column grid credits a turning move
  under standing material (a kerf to the axis) with everything above it
  (the same reason `LATHE_COLUMN_REFUSAL` refuses the column arm); any
  other kind ahead makes the prior unknown, so the raw stock stands.
  Dropped: a meridian (revolved field) prior - the right model, but the
  drill laws read a height; that is #109-sized. A twist-drill
  predecessor is now cut with its point cone (`cone` for Drill as for
  Taper), so a pilot's 118 deg point is not read as a flat floor; the
  nose radius joins the digest; every Drill (not only cross drills)
  stamps the stock it read; `cut_by` keeps a NaN raw height NaN; the
  prior reading pads its disk by half a cell diagonal, refuses (not
  clamps) a ring count past 1e5, and drops vertical-plane arcs from the
  nose-lowered path (lowering only the ends would bend them) - dropping a
  cut credits less, never more.

## #107 - unsaved changes: a dirty flag and a save prompt on exit (2026-11-07)

- **Chosen:** the document is dirty when the command history's undo
  depth differs from the depth recorded at the last save or load
  (`History::is_dirty` / `History::mark_clean` in `camcraft_app::commands`).
  Undo back to the saved point is clean again; a redo past it is dirty
  again; a fresh command while the saved state sits on the redo stack
  makes the saved point unreachable (`None`), so the same depth on a new
  branch stays dirty. `History::clear` (New, Open) starts clean. Ephemeral
  state (selection via `execute_ephemeral`, camera, hover, layout) never
  touches the history, so it never dirties.
- **Why on `History`, not `project::is_dirty(world)`:** the history lives
  in the UI's `State`, not in the world, and the flag is a property of the
  history position; putting it next to `undo`/`redo` keeps it exact by
  construction and still in the app layer. Cost to move: a thin
  `project::is_dirty(&History)` wrapper if a non-UI caller wants one.
- **UI:** the window title leads with `*` while dirty. New, Open (the
  dialog arm) and Quit over a dirty document are held in
  `State::unsaved_prompt` and an egui `Modal` asks Save / Don't Save /
  Cancel (Escape or the backdrop = Cancel); the answer is a queued
  `CommandKind::ResolveUnsaved`. Save without a path asks for one; a
  cancelled or failed save keeps the document and the app open. The
  window X now queues a Quit like Ctrl+Q (a shell whose GPU failed still
  closes at once, since it never drains the queue).
- **The shell is winit, not eframe:** the brief's
  `viewport().close_requested()` + `CancelClose` does not apply - the
  shell owns `WindowEvent::CloseRequested`, so it simply does not exit
  there.
- **Dropped:** guarding the headless `OpenProjectFile` / `SaveProjectFile`
  arms (scripts and tests drive them; a prompt there would hang a
  headless run); a dirty counter bumped per command (cannot know when an
  undo returns to the saved state); hashing the document (costly, and
  derived caches such as toolpaths would make it noisy).
## #103: a turned path's axial rapids judged in the meridian plane (partial)

- **Law.** `operation/turning_rapids.rs` no longer drops the column law's
  word on a turned op's axial rapids and stops there: it drops it and
  judges each axial rapid (no XY travel) in the meridian plane. The
  rapid's nose disc (nose radius less the gouge tolerance) must not meet
  material between its two stations: the part and the setup stock
  revolved about the fitted axis (silhouette envelope per station; a
  station-span x max-radius box where no silhouette reads), less this
  path's own earlier feeds' nose sweep (signed radius, mirrored, so a
  facing pass across the axis counts) and less the stock the program
  ahead faced (the #89 prior grid read revolved, asked only on a
  conviction; job.rs now collects the prior for the turned family too).
- **Chosen:** the declared stock revolved, not the part as stock. The
  turning kernels ignore the stock (rho_clear is the part's r_max + tol),
  so a bar wider than the part is a real crash on the first approach.
- **Found (held):** the lathe_post fixtures (and very likely the
  turning_bore / turning_contour ones) set a 40 mm box stock from Z 0 to
  40 round a 12 mm bar: their approaches at r 6.85 from Z 25 run inside
  that box, so they are convicted - real by the declared stock, which the
  kernels never cut. Owed: decide fixtures (stock the bar's size) vs a
  kernel that roughs from the stock; the groove/part (Mode::Revolve)
  kinds are inside the law's scope too and convict the same way.
- **Dropped:** a sim-side Revolve rapid law (the sim has no stock solid
  of revolution; the app has the frame and the prior); reading the stock
  bore (a tube stock reads solid - conservative, owed).

### #103 resumed: fixtures, not the law

- **Fixtures.** The lathe suites' 40 mm box stock (Z 0 up) round 12-20
  mm bars is replaced by bar-sized stock - a Cylinder of the bar's
  diameter over its Z span - in lathe_post (profile, groove/part; a
  `bar_world` helper), turning_contour (r 10 blank; the stepped r 6 bar
  gets its own r 6 world, `contour_world_in`), turning_blade,
  turning_form, turning_thread and turning_bore. The convictions were
  real against the declared box: the turning kernels never cut stock
  beyond the part, filed as #130. No NC golden changed.
- **One wiring fix, found by turning_form:** the nose disc is the
  tool's `nose_radius` only for Turning and Bore inserts (their moves
  carry the nose centre); a groove/thread blade or form gauge carries
  its tip with the body outward, so it is judged as the tip point (a
  form's `nose_radius` is its crown arc - read as a 6 mm ball it
  convicted every clean form traverse). Owed: a blade's band along the
  axis past the rapid's ends is not read.
- **Held: turning_bore (3 tests).** The boring ride's approach runs down
  the axis (r 0, Z 60 -> -10) into the bar. Against the declared solid
  bar that is a real crash (no pilot hole); against honest stock (a tube,
  or a drill ahead) the law still convicts it, because both readings
  fill the bore: the stock and the part are each read as their OUTER
  silhouette, and the lathe prior credits facing only. A boring op can
  therefore never post - a false refusal class the law must lose before
  #103 closes: read each body's meridian section (inner and outer
  radius per station), and credit an axial drill ahead.

### #103 closed out: the bore reads as air, a pilot drill ahead is credited

- **Annulus, not disc.** `operation/turning_outline.rs` reads the part
  and the stock per station as material between r_in and r_out: r_out
  from the turned silhouette (span fallback), r_in by ray parity from
  the axis point (Moller-Trumbore, four skewed directions, read a hair
  either side of the station so an end face's own plane never counts
  edge-on): an odd count in any direction is a core to the axis (r_in
  0), else r_in is the nearest wall (no wall: nothing there). A bored
  part's hole and a tube's bore are air; a Cylinder with no bore is
  solid to the axis. Cached per station; read only inside the outer
  skin and only after the cheap credits miss. Owed: cost on very large
  meshes (a facet scan per station read, span-filtered).
- **Pilot credit.** An axial Drill ahead in the setup (`rest::drills_ahead`,
  on a lathe too; drill_prior's facing-only prior unchanged) is a removed
  cylinder of the drill radius over its plunge's stations, its point a
  cone of the tool's tip angle (#89's drill atom). Off-axis holes credit
  nothing. Like the facing prior, the turned op's stamp does not digest
  the drill ahead (#109 scope).
- **turning_bore fixture:** the bored bar now has its pilot - an axial
  r 2 drill (AX0, a 70 mm flute DR-0400; names sort ahead of the bore
  ops, which is program order) from the top to Z -12, under the ride's
  -10 window. Chosen over a tube stock: the fixture models a finished
  bore in solid bar, and a pilot is how a bore pass starts. Pinned:
  `a_boring_approach_into_a_solid_bar_with_no_pilot_is_convicted_and_blocks_the_post`.

### #103 review (PR #135): the body, the band, arcs, the point

- **B1, the bar's body.** A Bore tool is judged by its nose disc (the
  cutting tip) AND its body: a disc of max(diameter, shank) / 2 about
  the nose in the meridian, carried up the axis by flute + shank length.
  A pilot credits only the body points inside its cylinder and cone, so
  a Ø10 bar down a Ø4 pilot is convicted (`a_ten_mm_bar_down_a_four_mm_pilot_is_convicted`).
  The turning_bore pilot is now Ø11 to Z -16 (its 118-degree point clear
  under the ride's -10 window). *Assumption:* the body is centred on the
  nose. A bar whose tip sits at its body's edge reaches a full diameter
  off the axis; the catalog does not say which, and the kernel puts the
  nose on the axis for the approach - if that geometry is wanted, the
  body offset joins the tool data (follow-up, not guessed here).
- **B2, the blade's band.** Groove / part / form tools sample ±width/2
  along the axis about the move (the band's centre); a thread samples
  its crest half-width. Pinned by the reviewer's scenario
  (`a_single_groove_at_the_bars_end_is_judged_across_its_band`: one 5 mm
  groove at the end of a bar running 2 mm past the part - convicted; the
  centre point alone is not).
- **S1:** arc feeds credit nothing (a threading half-turn's chord crosses
  the axis). Conservative; an arc's true sweep is owed if it ever
  false-convicts.
- **S3:** a drill with no stated point is read as 118 degrees, not flat
  (a flat point credits MORE); the DrillAhead doc says so.
- **S2** (a pilot deleted after the bore leaves it Ok) is #109's - a
  lathe pin was added there, not fixed here.

### #109: a verdict that reads earlier ops digests them

- **Chosen: the stamp, not a live re-check at the post.** Every op whose
  verdict reads the program ahead now writes the existing rest digest
  (`rest::prior_digest`, the same term Pocket3D and Drill already wrote)
  into its generation stamp, so editing, regenerating, deleting or
  reordering an earlier op of its setup marks it Stale, and the post
  gate - which already refuses Stale - refuses it. Which ops: Pocket3D,
  Drill and every op with no 3+2 frame (`drill_prior::reads_prior`) -
  exactly the set `job::collect_job` hands `verify_prior` (the prior
  acquittal) and the turned family's pilot/facing credits ride. The
  stale reason names the moved predecessor, the same story as Pocket3D's.
- **Dropped: re-running `acquit_by_prior` / `judge_axial_rapids` live at
  the post.** It would keep stamps unchurned, but the post would cut the
  prior grid (the costly half) for every op every post, and two
  readings of one verdict could disagree; the stamp is the one source.
- **Cost, accepted:** every non-first op of a saved project reads Stale
  once on load and clears on regenerate (release notes say so). A posed
  (3+2) op reads no prior and keeps its stamp bit-for-bit. The digest
  reads predecessors' cached paths, so an edited-but-not-regenerated
  predecessor is its own Stale (the post refuses it first), and the
  dependent goes Stale when it is regenerated.
- **RegenerateAll converges in one click (#145).** The digest made a
  frozen batch leave a dependent Stale behind a predecessor regenerated
  in the same batch (a second click). Chosen: rounds inside the
  constructor - stage every Stale op in program order, finish in
  parallel, write the round so the next reads it, stop when nothing is
  Stale (cap: the op count; an op still Stale is named in `skipped`),
  then invert every write so `apply` replays the batch as ONE undo unit.
  Dropped: staging strictly one op at a time (loses M5.3 B's parallel
  finish for independent ops) and leaving two clicks (a user hits it).
  The constructor now writes the world transiently and restores it;
  every caller builds and executes on the main thread.
- **#153 review B1: the path signature is stored at the write.**
  `schema::Toolpath` carries a private `sig` (`path_sig::of`, the old
  `rest::path_hash`) computed in `Toolpath::new`, its only constructor,
  so `prior_digest` reads one word per op ahead and clones nothing -
  O(M) cheap reads per `status_of`, not M full path clones. Chosen
  over a sibling component (every writer would have to keep two
  components in step) and a flecs on-set observer (none exist in app;
  hooks writing components mid-set were not worth the risk). Caches
  are rebuilt whole, never edited in place (the one test that spliced
  a move now rebuilds). N3: the kind tag joins the digest.
  N1: a round defers an op that reads the program ahead when an op
  ahead of it in its setup is staged in that round - each op generates
  once; setups still run side by side.
- Pins: `a_face_regenerated_shallower_marks_the_acquitted_contour_stale`,
  `one_regenerate_all_brings_a_dependent_pair_current`,
  `the_program_ahead_digest_moves_only_with_the_path`,
  `a_reorder_marks_the_dependent_stale`,
  `a_posed_op_keeps_its_stamp_when_the_program_ahead_moves`
  (vertical_rapid_stock), `a_pilot_deleted_or_made_shallower_after_the_bore_marks_it_stale`
  (turning_bore). turning_bore's fixture moved to `tests/common/bore.rs`
  to keep the suite under the 400-line law.

### #103 re-review B3: the bar's body lies toward the axis

- **Law.** The Bore body is no longer centred on the nose: the insert
  sits at the body's edge and the body lies toward the axis, signed
  radius [rho - d, rho] (d the body diameter, max of diameter and shank).
  A bar with its nose on the axis reaches a whole diameter off it.
  Supersedes the "centred" assumption above - the kernel's own ride (a
  Ø10 bar riding r 5.6 in a Ø12 wall) rules it out, as the reviewer
  showed.
- **Kernel** (`motion::turning::bore`). `BoreParams.bar_radius` (half the
  body diameter; 0 keeps the old on-axis rapids) puts the approach and
  the retract at nose r = bar_radius - nose/2 on the cutting side,
  clipped to the ride's own end radii: the bar spans
  [r - 2 bar_radius, r + nose], centred on the spindle, so a pilot just
  over the bar's size admits it. Chosen over r = bar_radius (the nose
  then pokes nose-radius past the body, into a Ø11 pilot with a 0.8
  nose) and over a full disc of radius d about the nose (convicts every
  honest bore). The off-wall retract is now radial to that line, not to
  the axis.
- **Fixture.** turning_bore keeps the Ø11 pilot to Z -16 (Ø10 body plus
  clearance, under the Ø12 finished bore; a 0.8 regrind still fits:
  ±5.4 inside 5.5). Pinned: `a_ten_mm_bar_with_its_nose_on_the_axis_in_an_eleven_mm_pilot_is_convicted`
  (law, nose on the axis convicted, the kernel's centred line clean) and
  motion's `a_stated_bar_enters_and_leaves_with_its_own_axis_on_the_spindle`.
  No golden carries a bore path; none changed.
- The law's unit pins moved to `operation/turning_rapids_tests.rs`
  (size budget).

### #103 re-review B4: head and shank modelled apart

- **Law and kernel share one shape**, `motion::turning::bar_spans`: the
  insert sits at the head's edge, so the head spans [-head_d, 0]
  outward of the nose, over `flute_len` up the axis. The shank is read
  both ways a tool record can mean it, with its edge on the insert's or
  its axis on the head's, and the union kept:
  [-max(shank_d, (head_d + shank_d)/2), max(0, (shank_d - head_d)/2)],
  over `shank_len` above the flute. A shank wider than the head reaches
  past the nose. `centred_nose` puts the kernel's rapids where the whole
  bar (head, shank and the nose past the head's edge) is centred on the
  spindle. `BoreParams.bar_radius` became `head_d` / `shank_d`.
- **Chosen:** modelling over refusing (a stepped-shank bar is an ordinary
  tool, per the coordinator), and the union over the coaxial reading
  alone. The union is conservative: the reviewer's Ø8/Ø12 bar centred
  spans 14 mm, so it is refused in a Ø13 pilot even though the coaxial
  reading (12 mm) would fit. The tool record does not say which reading
  holds. If that false refusal bites, an explicit shank-offset field
  joins the tool data.
- **Pins:** `a_bar_whose_shank_outgrows_its_head_is_judged_by_its_shank`
  (law: the reviewer's scenario convicted centred and on the old line,
  clean in a pilot it fits), `a_bar_whose_shank_outgrows_its_head_is_judged_by_its_full_shank`
  (app: fails when generate passes half the diameters, checked by
  reverting the line), and `a_twelve_mm_bar_in_the_eleven_mm_pilot_is_convicted`.
- **Filed:** #146, the bar's body during cutting feeds (P1).

## #117 - the cross drill is judged against the finished part (2026-11-07, Prime Directive)

- **Chosen:** the cross arm refuses by name (a `GenError`, so nothing
  posts) when the drill - its radius along the hole axis from the
  station to the tip, the point cone, shank and holder - enters the
  finished part's solid past `GOUGE_TOL` (the axial verdict's 0.01 mm).
  The judge is the verify crate's solid law (`solid_hits`, posed along
  each move's tool axis, `hole_walls` on), run on the finished world-
  frame chain in `cross_spindle::cross_drill` (`cross_part.rs`). A
  bisection of the offending plunge says how deep the tip got: less
  than one drill radius reads "the model has no hole there", deeper
  reads "runs past the modelled hole's floor".
- **Dropped:** a `Warning::Gouge` in the verify tail like
  `axial_warnings` (it names a move, not the hole, and every other
  radial law - reach, holder, rapids - already refuses by name in the
  arm); re-reading the holes by recognition (the radial recogniser
  reads YZ/XZ walls only; the swept solid judges any hole, any face).
- **Fixtures were wrong, not the law:** every cross suite drilled a
  solid bar with no modelled hole (22 tests convicted). They now model
  their holes (`tests/punched_bar`: a round bar with radial blind holes
  cut in, and a flat face with one hole). Three choices ride it:
  1. **Off the knife-edge:** the old r10 x 40 bar (L/D 2) sat exactly on
     the lathe axis reader's isotropy door (ISO = 0.5: caps' normal
     moment = half the face's), so any modelled hole was refused as
     "every axis fits" - filed as #152, the reader untouched here. The
     drilled bar runs z -80..20 (L/D 5; the top, z20, every Top-of-Part
     and end-face number rides, is unchanged), which also keeps the
     holes a small share of the surface the fit must find revolved.
  2. **Half-turn images:** one-sided holes tilt the robust axis fit by
     ~0.001 mm, past the spindle law's 0.0005 (the #116 band), so each
     modelled hole carries its image about Z (modelled, never drilled);
     two that meet on one line become one through hole.
  3. **Where the r10 bar cannot carry the hole** (an off-centre hole
     whose edge runs past the bar, y 7..11 or 6..12 - a notch, not a
     hole), the part is a small core the hole never reaches; the raw
     stock, wider, sets every standoff, so the chain is the same (the
     bit-for-bit fingerprints still hold). And the box suite's lump on
     the hole's line (a part poking out of the stock face) is split into
     four lumps in the CORNERS of the drill's square entry band: the
     entry still reads them, the round drill clears them - a lump in the
     drill's own path is now (rightly) a refused gouge.

## #106 - rapid-in-stock reads the tool's footprint, not its centre (2026-11-07)

- **Chosen:** law (d)'s column reading (the lateral rapid's a / mid / b
  samples and #96's vertical dive) asks `in_stock && below
  surface_before` at every sample of the tool's footprint disc of
  radius `r - gouge_tol` - the centre, 8 points at half radius, 16 on
  the rim - not at the centre alone. Any sample in stock and under the
  surface the earlier cuts left convicts. The disc and the sample count
  are the ones `rapids_radial` (#79) and `hidden_along` already use, so
  the mill laws read one tool.
- **Why `r - gouge_tol`:** a dive or link tangent to the stock wall (an
  approach at exactly r off the outline, a link riding its own kerf's
  edge) is not a collision; the full radius would convict it on
  rounding.
- **Left alone:** `acquit_by_prior` already reads the whole disc
  (radius r, the highest prior column under it), so it needed no
  change; the radial (`Mode::Radial`) reading already samples the flute
  body discs.
- **Dropped:** an exact disc-versus-polygon / disc-versus-kerf-union
  test (the kerf union is not built anywhere; sampling with the stated
  rim bound `r (1 - cos(pi/16))` matches the radial law's promise);
  sampling only the vertical law (the issue names both, and the lateral
  law had the same gap).
- **Review fix (PR #138, tip shape):** each footprint sample is judged
  at `z_tip + lift(rho)`, the height the tool's own tip stands at that
  radius - 0 for a square end or inside a bull's flat, the corner arc
  outside it (a ball is a bull with no flat), `rho / tan(half angle)`
  up a drill/taper point - against `surface_before`, which already
  caps at the stock top. The lift comes from the judged `Cutter`
  (`corner_r`, `tip_angle`; `Cutter::lift_at`), NOT
  `ToolGeom::nose_radius` as the review suggested: that field is the
  turning insert's nose and is 0.0 for every mill kind, so a ball mill
  would have read as square. A context with no stated tip is judged
  square, which can only over-report. Left as is: `surface_before`
  still treats every earlier cut as flat to radius r (the column
  model's own optimism near a ball pass's edge, review item 4), and
  the overhang backstop `hidden_along` still reads a flat disc - both
  are pre-existing and model-only.
- **Re-review fix (PR #138, radial gap):** three sample radii (centre,
  half, rim) let a wall that fell between the half ring and the rim be
  judged only by rim samples lifted almost a full corner - a real dive
  into the wall read clean (the earlier bull "clean" pin asserted a
  gouge). Now 8 rings at `d k / 8` with `2 k` points each (the rim's
  16 scaled by radius; 73 samples a station), and ring k is judged at
  ring k - 1's lift, the lowest the tool stands over the band between
  them. Dropped: an exact disc-versus-polygon minimum of the lifted
  surface (needs a lifted-tool / stock-edge distance per wall segment;
  the ring bound d / 8 plus the chord bulge is stated instead).

## #164: Idle window redraw and high CPU

- The reported project loads and processes through the CLI in under a second.
  The windowed shell currently uses `ControlFlow::Poll` and requests another
  redraw unconditionally after each frame, so an open project keeps rebuilding
  its scene and browser even when the user is idle.
- Choose event-driven redraw: request a frame for input and queued commands;
  honor egui's repaint delay for timed UI work; keep a bounded timer while
  simulation or import progress needs frames. An idle document then waits for
  an event. This targets the repeated work while preserving live playback.
- Review added one follow-up frame after input because the shell collects the
  scene before the UI can change browser eyes or toolpath visibility. Suspend
  frame timers while the window is occluded, then redraw when it becomes
  visible again; hidden surfaces have no useful picture to update.

## Model placement and existing stock

- Carry existing stock by the same rigid transform when its source is the
  moved model, or when the document has only one non-fixture part. This
  preserves the stock's position and orientation relative to the part, and
  keeps the model and stock placement change in one undo step.
- In a document with several parts, leave box and cylinder stock in place:
  a fitted stock can cover more than one part and has no stored source link.
  A from-model stock has that link and follows its named source.
- Dropped: refitting stock to the new world-axis bounding box on every model
  move. A refit would discard the stock orientation and placement the user
  already chose.

## Facing pick on a rotated part

- A picked face already gives the facing boundary. Only open chains and
  chain-only selections need whole-model and stock silhouettes, so skip
  their sixteen-section projections for face-only picks. A steep face is
  refused at the pick with the existing horizontal-face guidance.
- Canonicalize face boundary rings in linear time with minimum-rotation
  scans in both directions. The previous comparison rebuilt every rotated
  copy of the ring, quadratic work repeated by the Geometry panel.
- Dropped: a UI-only cache of the selection account. It would hide the
  repeated work but leave the same expensive path in command validation
  and generation.
- Follow-up from the edge-pick hand test: a Face operation can use an open
  chain, so its panel and viewport legitimately need the model and stock
  silhouettes. Cache the exact input/output of the shared sixteen-section
  projection for meshes up to 50,000 facets. Exact facet comparison avoids
  a digest collision becoming a wrong machining preview; a four-entry
  bound keeps the memory cost finite. Larger meshes use the original path.
- `CAMCRAFT_PROFILE_PROJECTION=1` reports projection cache misses with
  elapsed time and occasional hit counts. It is opt-in so a normal window
  does not spend time printing diagnostics on every read.

### #103 after merging #106 (rapid footprint): the facing approach and the lathe's radial rapids

- **Verdict on facing.nc's new 1/5/9/13/17 (inward `G00 X14.6 -> X11.6`
